P0300.m: The engine computer sees misfires that move around between cylinders instead of staying in one. The engine may shake, stumble or feel down on power. If the check engine light flashes, the misfire is bad enough to overheat the catalytic converter: slow down and get it checked right away.
c: Worn spark plugs or ignition coils
Low fuel pressure or dirty injectors

P0302.m: Cylinder 2 is not firing properly, so the engine runs rough and loses some power. A flashing check engine light means the misfire is serious enough to damage the catalytic converter, so slow down and get it checked right away.
c: Spark plug or ignition coil on cylinder 2

P1326.m: On Hyundai and Kia engines, the knock sensor detection system picked up vibration that can point to wearing connecting rod bearings. The car may go into limp mode. Owners are usually told to see a dealer, because this system was added during the brands' engine bearing campaigns.

P2111.t: Throttle Actuator Control System - Stuck Open
P2111.m: The electronic throttle is stuck more open than commanded. The car can go into limp mode or act unpredictably.

P0303.m: Cylinder 3 is not firing properly, so the engine runs rough and loses some power. A flashing check engine light means the misfire is serious enough to damage the catalytic converter, so slow down and get it checked right away.
c: Spark plug or ignition coil on cylinder 3

C1391.m: On Toyota and Lexus models with a powered brake booster (mostly hybrids), the brake computer saw the stored brake pressure falling faster than it should, which points to an internal leak. Braking assist can be affected, so get it checked before driving much.
c: Internal leak in the brake booster/accumulator assembly
Leaking seals in the brake actuator

P0304.m: Cylinder 4 is not firing properly, so the engine runs rough and loses some power. A flashing check engine light means the misfire is serious enough to damage the catalytic converter, so slow down and get it checked right away.
c: Spark plug or ignition coil on cylinder 4

P0420.m: The catalytic converter on bank 1 isn't cleaning the exhaust as well as it should. The car usually drives normally, but it can fail an emissions test.

P0301.m: Cylinder 1 is not firing properly, so the engine runs rough and loses some power. A flashing check engine light means the misfire is serious enough to damage the catalytic converter, so slow down and get it checked right away.
c: Spark plug or ignition coil on cylinder 1

P2112.t: Throttle Actuator Control System - Stuck Closed
P2112.m: The electronic throttle is stuck more closed than commanded, so the engine loses power and may go into limp mode.

C0020.m: The ABS module saw an electrical fault in the motor that runs the ABS pump. The ABS (and usually traction/stability) warning lights come on and anti-lock braking is switched off until it is fixed.
c: Worn or sticking ABS pump motor inside the hydraulic control unit (HCU)
Faulty ABS control module (ECU) if a new HCU does not clear it
Wiring or connector problem at the ABS unit

P2138.t: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch D/E Voltage Correlation
P2138.m: The two gas pedal position signals disagree, so the car may go into reduced power or not respond to the pedal.

P0700.m: The transmission computer found its own problem and asked for the check engine light. Another transmission code with the details is usually stored too.
c: A second transmission code that says what failed (the transmission computer has to be read for it)
A shift solenoid or sensor fault

P0463.t: Fuel Level Sensor A Circuit High
P0463.m: The fuel level sender reads too high. The gauge can show fuel that isn't there, which risks running out of gas.

U3000.m: A control module reports an internal failure. On the Hondas most named in complaints it is stored by the airbag (SRS) unit, so the airbag light comes on and the passenger airbag indicator can stay off.
c: Faulty front passenger seat weight sensor (2020-22 Odyssey/Pilot/Passport recall)
Internal fault in the SRS unit or another module

P0087.m: The engine isn't getting the fuel pressure it needs. That can cause hesitation, loss of power and stalling, especially under load.
c: Faulty fuel pressure sensor or regulator

P0017.t: Crankshaft Position - Camshaft Position Correlation (Bank 1 Sensor B)
P0017.m: The crankshaft and the bank 1 camshaft aren't lined up the way the computer expects. That usually points to timing chain or belt problems, so it's worth checking early before it gets worse.
c: Stretched timing chain or jumped belt

P0016.t: Crankshaft Position - Camshaft Position Correlation (Bank 1 Sensor A)
P0016.m: The crankshaft and the bank 1 camshaft aren't lined up the way the computer expects. That usually points to timing chain or belt problems, so it's worth checking early before it gets worse.
c: Stretched timing chain or jumped belt

P052E.t: Positive Crankcase Ventilation Regulator Valve Performance
P052E.m: The crankcase ventilation (PCV) system isn't controlling pressure the way it should.
c: Failed PCV valve or oil separator

P0720.m: The transmission lost its output speed signal. The speedometer and shifting can act up.

P1450.t: Unable to Bleed Up Fuel Tank Vacuum
P1450.m: On Fords, the fuel vapor (EVAP) system couldn't release vacuum from the gas tank. It's an emissions fault; the car usually drives normally.
c: Blocked EVAP vent valve or filter
Faulty purge valve (some Ford bulletins replace it)

P0456.t: Evaporative Emission System Leak Detected (Very Small Leak)
P0456.m: There's a very small leak in the fuel vapor system. The car drives normally.
c: Tiny crack in an EVAP hose

P0316.m: The engine misfired in the first moments after starting. It often shows up as a rough or shaky cold start.

P0171.m: Bank 1 is getting too much air or too little fuel. The engine may hesitate or idle rough.
c: Weak fuel pump or clogged filter

P0014.t: B Camshaft Position Timing Over-Advanced or System Performance (Exhaust, Bank 1)
P0014.m: The variable valve timing for the exhaust camshaft on bank 1 isn't where the computer asked it to be. The engine can idle rough, lose power or use more fuel. Low or dirty oil is a common trigger, because oil pressure moves the timing.
c: Low, old or wrong-grade engine oil

P0741.t: Torque Converter Clutch Solenoid Circuit Performance/Stuck Off
P0741.m: The torque converter isn't locking up as commanded. You may feel shudder or see higher RPM on the highway.

P0299.m: The turbo isn't making the boost the computer asked for, so the car feels slow and may go into reduced power.

P0722.t: Output Speed Sensor Circuit No Signal
P0722.m: There's no output speed signal from the transmission, so shifts and the speedometer can fail.

C2200.m: The ABS control module found a fault inside itself during its self-checks. The ABS, traction/stability and often brake warning lights come on and those systems are turned off.
c: Corroded or loose ABS module connector or poor ground
Brake fluid leaking into the electric parking-brake caliper wiring (C2200-48 case)

P2135.t: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch A/B Voltage Correlation
P2135.m: The two throttle position signals disagree, so the computer cuts power to stay safe.

P0430.m: The catalytic converter on bank 2 isn't cleaning the exhaust as well as it should.

P0740.m: The torque converter lockup solenoid has an electrical fault. Fuel economy drops and the car may shudder.

P0011.t: A Camshaft Position Timing Over-Advanced or System Performance (Intake, Bank 1)
P0011.m: The variable valve timing for the intake camshaft on bank 1 isn't where the computer asked it to be. The engine can idle rough, lose power or use more fuel. Low or dirty oil is a common trigger, because oil pressure moves the timing.
c: Low, old or wrong-grade engine oil

P0128.t: Coolant Thermostat (Coolant Temperature Below Thermostat Regulating Temperature)
P0128.m: The engine isn't reaching normal temperature fast enough. The heater may blow cool and fuel economy drops.

P0008.m: The engine computer sees the cam and crank timing drifting out of line on bank 1. On many engines this is an early sign of a stretched timing chain.
c: Faulty cam phaser or VVT solenoid

P2442.t: Secondary Air Injection System Switching Valve Stuck Open (Bank 2)
P2442.m: The valve that lets cold-start air into the bank 2 exhaust is stuck open. Exhaust moisture can then reach and damage the air pump.
c: Water or carbon in the valve

P0776.t: Pressure Control Solenoid B Performance/Stuck Off
P0776.m: Transmission pressure solenoid B isn't controlling pressure, so shifts can slip, flare or bang.

P0335.m: The computer lost or can't read the crankshaft position signal. Without it the engine can stall and may not restart.

P0172.m: Bank 1 is getting too much fuel. You may smell fuel or see worse mileage.

P0306.m: Cylinder 6 is not firing properly, so the engine runs rough and loses some power. A flashing check engine light means the misfire is serious enough to damage the catalytic converter, so slow down and get it checked right away.
c: Spark plug or ignition coil on cylinder 6

P2440.t: Secondary Air Injection System Switching Valve Stuck Open (Bank 1)
P2440.m: The valve that lets cold-start air into the bank 1 exhaust is stuck open. Exhaust moisture can then reach and damage the air pump.
c: Water or carbon in the valve

P0305.m: Cylinder 5 is not firing properly, so the engine runs rough and loses some power. A flashing check engine light means the misfire is serious enough to damage the catalytic converter, so slow down and get it checked right away.
c: Spark plug or ignition coil on cylinder 5

U0100.m: The other computers in the car stopped hearing from the engine computer. Features that depend on it can stop working, and several warning lights often come on together.
c: Wiring or connector fault on the data network
Power or ground problem at the engine computer

C14A7.t: AWD Power Transfer Unit Motor Blocked
C14A7.m: The all-wheel-drive computer commanded the power transfer unit (PTU) motor to move but it was blocked or did not move as expected. The driver sees a Service 4WD light or an 'AWD System Service Required' message and AWD/4WD may stop working.
c: Sticking or failed PTU (front axle disconnect) actuator motor
Binding inside the power transfer unit
Software that needs an update per the bulletin

P0730.m: The transmission isn't matching the expected engine-to-wheel speed in some gear, which usually means slipping.

B1448.m: The airbag computer sees a fault in the sensor mat under the front passenger seat cushion that decides whether an adult, child or nobody is sitting there. The airbag light comes on and the passenger airbag may not be set correctly.
c: Failed passenger seat occupant sensor mat
Damaged or loose wiring/connector under the passenger seat
Liquid spilled on the seat or electronics placed on the cushion (can set it temporarily)

P0340.m: The computer can't read the bank 1 camshaft position sensor. Expect hard starting, stalling or a rough run.

B1018.m: The airbag system found a fault in the front passenger seat occupant sensing parts (the weight/occupant sensor or its control unit). The airbag light comes on or flashes and the passenger airbag status may be wrong.
c: Failed occupant sensor or sensor mat in the passenger seat cushion
Loose connector or bad ground in the seat wiring

P0101.t: Mass or Volume Air Flow Sensor A Range/Performance
P0101.m: The air flow reading doesn't match what the computer expects. The engine may hesitate, stall or idle rough.

P0455.t: Evaporative Emission System Leak Detected (Large Leak)
P0455.m: There's a large leak in the fuel vapor system. Often it's just a gas cap left loose or off.
c: Purge or vent valve stuck open

U0101.m: The other computers in the car stopped hearing from the transmission computer. Features that depend on it can stop working, and several warning lights often come on together.
c: Wiring or connector fault on the data network
Power or ground problem at the transmission computer

C1256.m: The brake computer saw that the stored hydraulic pressure that powers the brakes stayed too low. The brake warning light comes on, a buzzer may sound, and the brake pedal can feel different.
c: Internal leak in the brake actuator / accumulator assembly
Worn brake booster pump motor that can't build pressure
Faulty accumulator pressure sensor inside the actuator

U0401.m: Another computer in the car received data from the engine computer that did not make sense.
c: A fault inside the engine computer

B2278.m: The power steering computer has found a problem with the torque sensor that measures how hard you turn the wheel, so it drops into manual steering mode. The driver suddenly feels heavy steering, usually with a warning light or message.
c: Noisy or failing steering torque sensor
Power steering module software that needs the recall update
Wiring or connector problem at the steering column sensor

P1299.m: On Fords, the engine got hot enough that the computer turned on its overheat protection, which can shut off cylinders and cut power. Pull over and let it cool.

P129F.t: Fuel Pump Power Control Module Fuel Pump Speed Signal Incorrect
P129F.m: The engine computer is getting a wrong fuel pump speed report from the module that powers the fuel pump. Drivers report a check engine light, crank-no-start, stalling or rough running; some see the pump or electrical items stay on after shut-off.
c: Internal short in the K111 fuel pump driver / fuel pump power control module
Wrong software in a replacement fuel pump control module
Fuel pump or wiring fault (often set with P023F)

C0545.t: Power Steering Torque Sensor / Assist Fault
C0545.m: The electric power steering computer found a problem with the signal that measures how hard the driver is turning the wheel. It shows a Service Power Steering message and steering assist can be reduced or lost, making the wheel heavy.
c: Failed steering torque sensor or steering column/gear assembly
Internal interference inside the electric steering gear (2020-21 GM SUVs)

B0081.m: The airbag system found a fault with the passenger seat sensor that decides whether the front passenger airbag should be on or off. The airbag warning light comes on and the passenger airbag may be switched off.
c: Passenger seat connector not fully seated or loose terminals
Communication fault between the seat sensor module and the airbag module
Failed seat sensor mat or module needing calibration or replacement

P0747.t: Pressure Control Solenoid A Stuck On
P0747.m: The main transmission pressure solenoid is stuck on, so shifts can be harsh.

P219A.m: One or more cylinders on bank 1 are getting a different air-fuel mix than the others. The engine may idle rough or hesitate.

P0717.t: Input/Turbine Speed Sensor A Circuit No Signal
P0717.m: There's no input speed signal from the transmission.

B0020.t: Front Left Side Air Bag Module Circuit
B0020.m: The airbag computer found an open or short in the wiring to the driver-side front seat side airbag. The airbag light stays on and that side airbag may not deploy.
c: Loose or corroded connector under the driver seat
Failed driver-side seat side airbag module

P2106.t: Throttle Actuator Control System - Forced Limited Power
P2106.m: The computer found a throttle problem and put the car in limp mode with reduced power.

P0010.t: A Camshaft Position Actuator Circuit (Intake, Bank 1)
P0010.m: The variable valve timing for the intake camshaft on bank 1 isn't where the computer asked it to be. The engine can idle rough, lose power or use more fuel. Low or dirty oil is a common trigger, because oil pressure moves the timing.
c: Low, old or wrong-grade engine oil

P0174.m: Bank 2 is getting too much air or too little fuel.
c: Weak fuel pump or clogged filter

P0442.t: Evaporative Emission System Leak Detected (Small Leak)
P0442.m: There's a small leak in the fuel vapor system.

P0706.t: Transmission Range Sensor A Circuit Range/Performance
P0706.m: The gear selector position signal doesn't make sense. Shifting and starting can act up.

P0705.t: Transmission Range Sensor A Circuit (PRNDL Input)
P0705.m: The computer can't tell which gear the shifter is in. The car may not start, or may show the wrong gear.

P1098.m: The engine computer found the electric coolant control valve is not working right. The check engine light comes on and the cooling fans may run hard or keep running after the engine is shut off.
c: Failed or sticking engine coolant control/flow valve
Contaminated or corroded electrical connection at the valve
Engine computer software that needs an update

C1179.m: The ABS/brake control unit sees a bad signal from the delta stroke sensor that measures brake pedal travel on the active brake booster. Brake, ABS and stability warning lights come on and brake assist features may be limited.
c: Failed delta stroke sensor (built into the brake booster)
Open or shorted wiring between the sensor and ABS unit

C1252.t: Brake Booster Pump Motor on Time Abnormally Long
C1252.m: The pump that pressurizes the brake system ran much longer than it should, which usually means pressure is leaking away. Brake and ABS warning lights come on.
c: Internal leak in the brake actuator / booster assembly
Low brake fluid or air in the system

P0401.t: Exhaust Gas Recirculation A Flow Insufficient Detected
P0401.m: Not enough exhaust gas is being sent back into the engine. It can cause pinging and higher emissions.

P0012.t: A Camshaft Position Timing Over-Retarded (Intake, Bank 1)
P0012.m: The variable valve timing for the intake camshaft on bank 1 isn't where the computer asked it to be. The engine can idle rough, lose power or use more fuel. Low or dirty oil is a common trigger, because oil pressure moves the timing.
c: Low, old or wrong-grade engine oil

P0707.t: Transmission Range Sensor A Circuit Low
P0707.m: The gear selector position signal is too low.

P1778.m: The transmission computer sees that the CVT is not changing ratio the way it commanded through the step motor. The check engine light comes on and the car may feel sluggish or slow to speed up.
c: Failed or sticking CVT step motor
Problem in the CVT control valve body
Wiring or connector fault to the step motor

P061B.t: Internal Control Module Torque Calculation Performance
P061B.m: The engine computer's two torque calculations don't match, so it may cut power for safety.

P0217.m: The engine is overheating. Pull over safely and shut it off: driving an overheating engine can warp or crack it.

P0018.t: Crankshaft Position - Camshaft Position Correlation (Bank 2 Sensor A)
P0018.m: The crankshaft and the bank 2 camshaft aren't lined up the way the computer expects. That usually points to timing chain or belt problems, so it's worth checking early before it gets worse.
c: Stretched timing chain or jumped belt

U0121.t: Lost Communication With Anti-Lock Brake System (ABS) Control Module
U0121.m: The other computers in the car stopped hearing from the anti-lock brake (ABS) module. Features that depend on it can stop working, and several warning lights often come on together.
c: Wiring or connector fault on the data network
Power or ground problem at the anti-lock brake (ABS) module

P0441.t: Evaporative Emission System Incorrect Purge Flow
P0441.m: Fuel vapor isn't being drawn into the engine the way it should.

P2716.m: Transmission pressure solenoid D has an electrical fault.

U0415.t: Invalid Data Received From Anti-Lock Brake System (ABS) Control Module
U0415.m: Another computer in the car received data from the anti-lock brake (ABS) module that did not make sense.
c: A fault inside the anti-lock brake (ABS) module

P1285.m: On Fords, the cylinder head temperature sensor saw the engine overheating. Stop and let it cool before driving on.

P0606.m: The engine computer found a fault in its own processor. Stalling or limp mode can follow.
c: Poor power or ground to the module

C1253.t: Hydro Booster Pump Motor Relay Malfunction
C1253.m: The brake computer found a problem with the relay that switches the brake pressure pump on and off. Brake and ABS warning lights come on, and power-assisted braking can be reduced.
c: Failed ABS motor relay (ABS MTR or ABS MTR 2)
Wiring or connector fault in the pump relay circuit

U0140.t: Lost Communication With Body Control Module
U0140.m: The other computers in the car stopped hearing from the body control module. Features that depend on it can stop working, and several warning lights often come on together.
c: Wiring or connector fault on the data network
Power or ground problem at the body control module

P2119.t: Throttle Actuator Control Throttle Body Range/Performance
P2119.m: The throttle isn't reaching the position it's commanded to.

P0732.m: Second gear isn't matching the expected engine-to-wheel speed, which usually means slipping in that gear.

P0106.t: Manifold Absolute Pressure/Barometric Pressure Sensor Range/Performance
P0106.m: The MAP sensor reading doesn't fit what the engine is doing.

P2101.t: Throttle Actuator A Control Motor Circuit Range/Performance
P2101.m: The electronic throttle motor isn't responding correctly. The car may drop into reduced power.

P0868.m: Transmission fluid pressure is too low, which can cause slipping or loss of drive.

U0073.t: Control Module Communication Bus A Off
U0073.m: A data network the car's computers share has gone quiet.

P0731.m: First gear isn't matching the expected engine-to-wheel speed, which usually means slipping in that gear.

P1101.m: The engine computer compared airflow from its sensors with what it expected and they don't agree, usually from an air leak after the mass airflow sensor. The check engine light comes on and the engine may go into reduced power.
c: Charge air cooler outlet tube come loose from the throttle body (1.5L turbo)
Intake leak from a cracked or loose duct, hose or clamp
Dirty or faulty mass airflow sensor

P06DD.t: Engine Oil Pressure Control Circuit Stuck Off
P06DD.m: Oil pressure isn't reaching what the computer asked for; the variable oil pump may be stuck in its low-pressure mode. Check the oil level and have the oil pressure tested right away.

P2122.t: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch D Circuit Low
P2122.m: One of the gas pedal position signals reads too low, so the car may go into reduced power.

B0111.t: Open in Side Squib RH Circuit
B0111.m: The airbag computer found a broken circuit to the right-side (passenger side) seat airbag igniter. The airbag light stays on, and that side airbag may not deploy in a crash.
c: Damaged or loose floor wiring harness / connector under the right front seat

P1682.m: The engine computer gets two ignition-on power feeds and found they don't match. Drivers can see stalling, a reduced engine power message, misfire-like running and several warning lights.
c: Poor terminal tension or corrosion at the underhood fuse block (terminal 51, X3 connector on Traverse/Acadia/Enclave)
Loose connection in the underhood electrical center
Ignition switch or ignition feed wiring fault (less common)

U0402.m: Another computer in the car received data from the transmission computer that did not make sense.
c: A fault inside the transmission computer

B00A0.m: The front passenger occupant classification system (the seat sensor that tells the airbag who is sitting there) has a fault. The airbag light comes on and the passenger airbag status may be wrong.
c: OCS needs a zero-point reset after seat work
Failed OCS control unit or seat sensor
Wiring or low voltage to the OCS unit

P0440.m: The system that traps fuel vapor from the gas tank has a fault. It's an emissions problem, not usually a drivability one.

P0500.m: The computer lost the vehicle speed signal. The speedometer, cruise control and shifting can act up.
c: ABS sensor fault on some cars

P0607.m: The engine computer isn't performing correctly.

C1247.m: The brake/stability computer got a bad signal from the sensor that measures how far the brake pedal is pressed. ABS, brake and VSC warning lights can come on.
c: Faulty brake pedal stroke sensor or wrong sensor adjustment
Wiring or connector problem at the sensor
Skid control computer software logic (Sequoia bulletin fix)

P2714.t: Pressure Control Solenoid D Performance/Stuck Off
P2714.m: Transmission pressure solenoid D isn't controlling pressure, so shifts can slip or bang.

P0089.m: The fuel pressure regulator isn't holding the pressure the computer asks for. Stalling and hesitation are common.

P0746.t: Pressure Control Solenoid A Performance/Stuck Off
P0746.m: The main transmission pressure solenoid isn't controlling pressure, so shifts can slip or flare.

U0131.t: Lost Communication With Power Steering Control Module
U0131.m: The other computers in the car stopped hearing from the power steering control module. Features that depend on it can stop working, and several warning lights often come on together.
c: Wiring or connector fault on the data network
Power or ground problem at the power steering control module

P0733.m: Third gear isn't matching the expected engine-to-wheel speed, which usually means slipping in that gear.

P2104.t: Throttle Actuator Control System - Forced Idle
P2104.m: The computer found a throttle problem and is holding the engine at idle for safety. The car may barely move.

B1342.m: A control module has run a self-check and found a fault inside itself. Which module depends on the car; on 2008-2011 Escape/Mariner it is usually the electric power steering module, and the driver may lose power steering assist.
c: Internal failure of the module that stored the code
On 2008-2011 Escape/Mariner: failed power steering control module (fixed by replacing the steering column)
Low or unstable supply voltage to the module

P0841.t: Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch A Circuit Range/Performance
P0841.m: A transmission fluid pressure reading doesn't match the gear the computer expects.

C1223.m: The stability control (VSC) system turned itself off because the ABS side of the brake computer reported a fault. VSC/TRAC and ABS warning lights come on; it usually points to another ABS code.
c: Another stored ABS fault, such as a wheel speed sensor or pump problem
Wiring problem in the ABS system

P0780.m: A shift didn't happen the way the computer expected.

P0336.m: The crankshaft position signal is erratic. The engine can stumble, stall or be hard to start.

P0369.t: Camshaft Position Sensor B Circuit Intermittent (Bank 1)
P0369.m: The second cam sensor signal on bank 1 drops out now and then.

P0734.m: Fourth gear isn't matching the expected engine-to-wheel speed, which usually means slipping in that gear.

P0446.t: Evaporative Emission System Vent Control Circuit
P0446.m: The EVAP vent valve isn't working right.

P0021.t: A Camshaft Position Timing Over-Advanced or System Performance (Intake, Bank 2)
P0021.m: The variable valve timing for the intake camshaft on bank 2 isn't where the computer asked it to be. The engine can idle rough, lose power or use more fuel. Low or dirty oil is a common trigger, because oil pressure moves the timing.
c: Low, old or wrong-grade engine oil

B1706.m: The airbag computer reads too much resistance in the circuit of the passenger seat belt buckle pretensioner (the charge that pulls the belt tight in a crash). The airbag light comes on.
c: Loose or poorly mating connector under the passenger seat
Worn or faulty passenger seat belt buckle assembly

P0744.t: Torque Converter Clutch Solenoid Circuit Intermittent
P0744.m: The torque converter lockup control drops out now and then.

U0416.t: Invalid Data Received From Vehicle Dynamics Control Module
U0416.m: Another computer in the car received data from the stability control module that did not make sense.
c: A fault inside the stability control module

P0496.t: Evaporative Emission System High Purge Flow
P0496.m: Too much fuel vapor is being pulled into the engine, often from a purge valve stuck open. It can cause hard starts after fueling.

U0420.t: Invalid Data Received From Power Steering Control Module
U0420.m: Another computer in the car received data from the power steering control module that did not make sense.
c: A fault inside the power steering control module

P0507.t: Idle Air Control System RPM Higher Than Expected
P0507.m: The engine idles higher than it should.

P0715.m: The transmission lost its input speed signal, so shifting can become harsh or stuck in one gear.

P0711.t: Transmission Fluid Temperature Sensor A Circuit Range/Performance
P0711.m: The transmission fluid temperature reading doesn't make sense.

P050A.t: Cold Start Idle Air Control System Performance
P050A.m: Right after a cold start, the idle speed isn't where the computer wants it.

P25A2.t: Brake System Control Module A Requested MIL Illumination
P25A2.m: The brake (ABS) control module found a fault of its own and asked the engine computer to turn on the check engine light. This code is a messenger: the real problem is in a brake-module code stored alongside it.
c: A fault stored in the ABS/brake module (wheel speed sensor, pump, valve)
Wiring or connector problems at the brake module

P0A43.t: Drive Motor A Position Sensor Circuit Intermittent
P0A43.m: On a hybrid or EV, the sensor that tells the computer exactly where the electric drive motor's rotor is sent a signal that cut in and out. The hybrid system may light warnings, limit power or shut down drive.
c: Loose or corroded connector at the motor position sensor (resolver)
Damaged wiring between the sensor and the inverter/control module
Failing position sensor in the drive motor

U1000.m: A module stopped hearing (or sending) expected messages on the car's CAN data network. Warning lights and features run by that module can drop out, often several at once.
c: Open or shorted CAN wiring or a loose connector
A module unplugged during a repair
Low battery voltage or bad ground

P0121.m: The throttle position reading doesn't make sense for the conditions. Hesitation or reduced power is common.

P0024.t: B Camshaft Position Timing Over-Advanced or System Performance (Exhaust, Bank 2)
P0024.m: The variable valve timing for the exhaust camshaft on bank 2 isn't where the computer asked it to be. The engine can idle rough, lose power or use more fuel. Low or dirty oil is a common trigger, because oil pressure moves the timing.
c: Low, old or wrong-grade engine oil

P0191.t: Fuel Rail Pressure Sensor A Range/Performance
P0191.m: The fuel pressure reading doesn't match what the computer expects. Hard starting or stalling can follow.

B1650.m: The airbag computer got a fault from the passenger-seat sensor that decides whether someone is sitting there. The airbag light comes on and the front passenger airbag may be switched off even with an adult in the seat.
c: Liquid spilled on the passenger seat or high humidity reaching the sensor mat
Loose or poor contact in the seat sensor (ODS) harness
Faulty seat sensor mat or occupant detection module

U3003.m: A module saw supply voltage outside its normal range, usually too low. Features run by that module (stability control, steering assist, hybrid 12V charging) can switch off or show warnings until voltage recovers.
c: Loose or corroded battery cables or grounds

C1241.t: Low or High Battery Voltage (Brake/Stability Computer)
C1241.m: The brake/ABS computer saw its supply voltage go too low (or too high). ABS, brake and stability warning lights come on until the voltage is normal again.
c: Weak 12-volt battery or poor battery terminals
Blown fuse, bad relay or wiring in the ABS power supply

P1E00.t: Hybrid Control Module Requested Check Engine Light
P1E00.m: This is a 'messenger' code: the Volt's hybrid control module found a fault and asked the engine computer to turn on the check engine light. The real problem is in a separate hybrid/charging code; GM's bulletin links it to charges that were cut short or interrupted.
c: Charging was interrupted (power loss, brown-out, or unplug/re-plug of the charge cord)
Another stored hybrid or high-voltage code (e.g. P0D3E) that needs its own diagnosis

U0155.t: Lost Communication With Instrument Panel Cluster (IPC) Control Module
U0155.m: The other computers in the car stopped hearing from the instrument cluster. Features that depend on it can stop working, and several warning lights often come on together.
c: Wiring or connector fault on the data network
Power or ground problem at the instrument cluster

P17F1.m: On Nissans with a CVT, the transmission computer detected judder. Nissan's repair steps for this code inspect the control valve (valve body) and the CVT's belt or chain.

P17F0.m: On Nissans with a CVT, the transmission computer detected shudder (judder) while driving. Nissan service bulletins send this code to a transmission inspection, and some cars got a reprogram or a new CVT.

P1327.m: The engine computer's piston ring noise sensing software heard vibration that points to damage on the piston oil rings. The check engine light comes on and Kia's fix is often a replacement engine.
c: Piston oil ring damage and cylinder wall wear in the 2.0L Nu MPI engine
Engine oil consumption from ring damage
Rarely a sensing fault, which is why the software update is done first

B1B02.m: The airbag computer sees a broken (open) circuit to the driver's front airbag. The airbag light comes on and the driver airbag may not deploy in a crash.
c: Failed clockspring in the steering column
Loose or damaged connector at the steering wheel airbag
Broken wiring between the airbag module and the steering column

P2196.t: O2 Sensor Signal Biased/Stuck Rich (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
P2196.m: The upstream O2 sensor keeps reading rich.

U0418.t: Invalid Data Received From Brake System Control Module
U0418.m: Another computer in the car received data from the brake system control module that did not make sense.
c: A fault inside the brake system control module

P008A.t: Low Pressure Fuel System Pressure - Too Low
P008A.m: The computer saw that the low-pressure side of the fuel system (the in-tank pump feeding the high-pressure pump) is not delivering enough pressure. Expect weak power, hesitation, hard starts or stalling.
c: Weak or failing in-tank (low-pressure) fuel pump
Clogged fuel filter or restricted fuel line

P1702.m: The engine/transmission computer saw the gear-position (PRNDL) sensor signal drop out or jump around for a moment. Drivers may notice harsh or wrong shifts, a flashing O/D light, or starting trouble in Park/Neutral.
c: Worn or misadjusted transmission range sensor
Loose or corroded connector at the range sensor
Damaged wiring between the sensor and the computer

P0725.m: The transmission computer lost the engine speed signal.

P2110.t: Throttle Actuator Control System - Forced Limited RPM
P2110.m: The computer is limiting engine speed because of a throttle fault.

C200D.m: The electric power steering module found that the sensor reading the steering motor's position has failed. Power assist is removed, so the steering turns heavy and a warning shows on the dash.
c: Failed motor position sensor inside the electric steering gear
Internal fault in the power steering assembly

B141B.t: Second-Row Left Inflatable Seat Belt Circuit Fault
B141B.m: The airbag computer found a problem in the wiring to the left (driver-side) second-row inflatable seat belt, so it turns on the airbag warning light. That belt's airbag may not deploy in a crash until it is fixed.
c: Worn or broken wires in the second-row seat harness (often from folding the seat)
Damaged connector at the base of the left second-row seat

P219B.m: One or more cylinders on bank 2 are getting a different air-fuel mix than the others. The engine may idle rough or hesitate.

P1870.m: On GM automatics like the 4L60-E, the computer saw slipping when the torque converter clutch was told to lock up, most often from wear in the torque converter clutch valves.
c: Worn TCC regulator or isolator valve bore

P0102.t: Mass or Volume Air Flow Sensor A Circuit Low
P0102.m: The air flow sensor signal is too low.

C1277.m: The ABS/stability computer lost a good steering-wheel angle signal. Stability and traction control are switched off and warning lights come on; on 2010-era Fusions it often shows up alongside a power steering fault.
c: Faulty steering wheel angle sensor or its wiring
Electric power steering fault that stops the steering signals (Fusion)
Steering parts out of spec, such as worn front lower control arms (Fusion)

B1801.t: Open in Driver Side Squib Circuit
B1801.m: The airbag computer found a broken circuit to the driver's front airbag igniter in the steering wheel. The airbag light stays on and the driver airbag may not deploy in a crash.
c: Worn or broken spiral cable (clock spring) in the steering column
Wiring or connector fault, or a faulty airbag sensor module

P2441.t: Secondary Air Injection System Switching Valve Stuck Closed (Bank 1)
P2441.m: The valve that lets cold-start air into the bank 1 exhaust is stuck closed.
c: Water or carbon in the valve

C1963.m: The ABS module has switched off stability control because a signal it needs (often steering angle) is missing or bad. The traction/stability warning light comes on; normal braking still works.
c: Steering angle sensor or steering signal fault (often set together with C1277)
Electric power steering fault removing steering data
Network/communication faults to the ABS module

P3497.m: The system that shuts off cylinders to save fuel has a fault on bank 2.

P3400.m: The system that shuts off cylinders to save fuel has a fault on bank 1. The engine can run rough or misfire.

P0721.m: The transmission's output speed signal is erratic.

P0365.m: The computer can't read the second (usually exhaust) cam sensor on bank 1.

P1744.t: Torque Converter Clutch Solenoid Circuit Performance
P1744.m: The computer commanded the torque converter lockup clutch, but engine and transmission speeds show it is not applying or holding as expected. Drivers may feel shudder, slipping at cruise, or higher RPM and worse fuel economy; the check engine light comes on.
c: Worn or sticking torque converter clutch
Faulty TCC solenoid or valve body problem

U0151.t: Lost Communication With Restraints Control Module
U0151.m: The other computers in the car stopped hearing from the airbag (restraints) control module. Features that depend on it can stop working, and several warning lights often come on together.
c: Wiring or connector fault on the data network
Power or ground problem at the airbag (restraints) control module

P0716.t: Input/Turbine Speed Sensor A Circuit Range/Performance
P0716.m: The transmission's input speed signal is erratic.

P0341.m: The bank 1 camshaft signal doesn't match what the computer expects.
c: Stretched timing chain or jumped belt

P0755.m: Shift solenoid B isn't working as commanded, so the transmission may skip gears, shift harshly or stay in one gear.

P0019.t: Crankshaft Position - Camshaft Position Correlation (Bank 2 Sensor B)
P0019.m: The crankshaft and the bank 2 camshaft aren't lined up the way the computer expects. That usually points to timing chain or belt problems, so it's worth checking early before it gets worse.
c: Stretched timing chain or jumped belt

B1760.m: The passenger-seat occupant sensor mat reported a fault, so the car can't reliably tell who is sitting there. The airbag light comes on and the front passenger airbag may be switched off.
c: Liquid or rain water soaked into the passenger seat cushion
Poor contact in the seat sensor mat harness connector
Faulty sensor mat or seat cushion assembly

P07A3.t: Transmission Friction Element A Stuck On
P07A3.m: In an automatic transmission, clutch/friction element A is staying applied when the computer wants it released. Shifts can be harsh, the car can feel like it is binding, or the transmission may go into limp mode.
c: Low, old or contaminated transmission fluid
Stuck valve or solenoid in the valve body
Worn or damaged internal clutch parts

P050D.m: The engine idles rough right after a cold start.

P07F7.m: In 10th gear, the transmission's input and output speeds don't match the ratio 10th gear should give, so the transmission is slipping or not fully in that gear. Drivers notice slipping, flare or harsh/late shifts at highway speed.
c: Worn or slipping clutch pack used in 10th gear
Internal hydraulic leak or valve body problem

P0462.t: Fuel Level Sensor A Circuit Low
P0462.m: The fuel level sender reads too low. The gauge may show empty when it isn't, or the other way around.

P2096.t: Post Catalyst Fuel Trim System Too Lean (Bank 1)
P2096.m: After the catalytic converter, the exhaust reads too lean for too long.

P2757.t: Torque Converter Clutch Pressure Control Solenoid Control Circuit Performance/Stuck Off
P2757.m: The torque converter clutch pressure control isn't working as commanded. Shudder is common.

P2004.t: Intake Manifold Runner Control Stuck Open (Bank 1)
P2004.m: The flaps inside the bank 1 intake manifold are stuck open. Power and smoothness can suffer.
c: Carbon buildup on the runner flaps

P1604.m: The engine computer recorded that the engine took too long to start or wouldn't start normally. Drivers notice long cranking or a hard start, with the check engine light on.
c: Weak fuel pump or low fuel pressure
Engine computer software (Toyota bulletin update on some trucks)
Ignition, air intake or sensor faults that make starting hard

P144A.t: Evaporative Emission System Purge Vapor Line Restricted/Blocked
P144A.m: The computer found that fuel vapor is not flowing through the purge line from the charcoal canister to the engine as expected. The check engine light comes on; some owners also notice rough running or hard starting after refueling.
c: Stuck or failing canister purge valve
Kinked, blocked or collapsed purge hose

P090C.t: Clutch B Actuator Control Circuit Low
P090C.m: On an automated manual or dual-clutch transmission, the computer sees voltage that is too low in the circuit that drives the actuator for clutch B. The car may not shift, stall when stopping, get stuck in a gear or go into limp mode.
c: Failed clutch B actuator motor or solenoid
Damaged wiring or connector, or a short to ground
Blown fuse or poor module ground

U0001.m: The main high-speed data network that the car's computers use to talk has a fault. Many warning lights can come on at once.
c: Wiring or connector fault on the network
A failing module dragging the network down

P00C6.t: Fuel Rail Pressure Too Low - Engine Cranking
P00C6.m: Fuel pressure is too low while the engine is cranking, so it may be slow or unable to start.

P26A3.t: Engine Coolant Bypass Valve A Range/Performance
P26A3.m: The electronically controlled coolant valve (thermostat-style control valve) isn't moving to or reporting the position the computer asks for. The engine may warm up slowly, run too cool or hot, or give poor heater output.
c: Failing coolant control valve (Subaru calls it the thermo control valve)
Coolant vapor or leaks damaging the valve's sensor
Wiring or connector problem at the valve

P0404.t: Exhaust Gas Recirculation A Control Circuit Range/Performance
P0404.m: The EGR valve isn't moving the way it's commanded.

P1320.m: The engine computer is not getting the expected signal back from the ignition coil primary circuit, so it thinks one or more cylinders did not fire properly. The check engine light comes on, often with misfires or spark knock.
c: Failed ignition coil (often with a built-in power transistor)
Wiring or connector fault in a coil circuit
Crank or cam sensor problems disturbing the ignition trigger

P0796.t: Pressure Control Solenoid C Performance/Stuck Off
P0796.m: Transmission pressure solenoid C isn't controlling pressure.

P0013.t: B Camshaft Position Actuator Circuit (Exhaust, Bank 1)
P0013.m: The variable valve timing for the exhaust camshaft on bank 1 isn't where the computer asked it to be. The engine can idle rough, lose power or use more fuel. Low or dirty oil is a common trigger, because oil pressure moves the timing.
c: Low, old or wrong-grade engine oil

P200A.m: The intake runner flaps aren't moving as commanded.

P0520.t: Engine Oil Pressure Sensor/Switch A Circuit
P0520.m: The oil pressure sensor has an electrical fault. Check the real oil level before driving on.

P0234.m: The turbo is making more boost than it should, so the computer may cut power.

P0601.t: Internal Control Module Memory Check Sum Error
P0601.m: The engine computer found an error in its own memory.

C1203.m: The brake/stability computer isn't getting proper messages from the engine computer, so stability control shuts off. The VSC/TRAC warning lights come on.
c: Communication fault between the engine computer and skid control computer
Software/logic issue fixed by a Toyota bulletin (2003 Sequoia)
Wrong or mismatched replacement computer installed

B1382.t: Side Airbag Front Passenger Resistance Too High
B1382.m: The airbag computer reads too much resistance in the circuit of the passenger front seat side airbag. The airbag light comes on and that side airbag may not deploy.
c: Loose or high-resistance side airbag connector under the passenger seat

B0014.t: Driver Seat Side Air Bag Deployment Loop
B0014.m: The airbag computer sees a wiring fault (open, short, or wrong resistance) in the circuit to the side airbag built into the driver's seat. The airbag light comes on and that airbag may not deploy.
c: Loose or rubbing airbag connector under the driver's seat

P0344.t: Camshaft Position Sensor A Circuit Intermittent (Bank 1)
P0344.m: The bank 1 camshaft signal drops out now and then.

P0562.m: The car's electrical voltage is too low. Lights and modules may act up, and the car may not start next time.

P0506.t: Idle Air Control System RPM Lower Than Expected
P0506.m: The engine idles lower than it should and may stall.

U0293.t: Lost Communication With Hybrid Powertrain Control Module
U0293.m: The other computers in the car stopped hearing from the hybrid powertrain control module. Features that depend on it can stop working, and several warning lights often come on together.
c: Wiring or connector fault on the data network
Power or ground problem at the hybrid powertrain control module

P2127.t: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch E Circuit Low
P2127.m: The second gas pedal position signal reads too low.

P0777.t: Pressure Control Solenoid B Stuck On
P0777.m: Transmission pressure solenoid B is stuck on.

P228C.t: Fuel Pressure Regulator 1 Exceeded Control Limits - Pressure Too Low
P228C.m: The fuel pressure regulator can't keep pressure up. Stalling and power loss are common.
c: Failing fuel pump or high-pressure pump

B0074.m: The passenger seat sensor that tells the airbag system if someone is sitting there has a circuit fault. The airbag warning message comes on and the passenger airbag may be turned off.
c: Seat sensor mat connector loose or disengaged over time
Open or high resistance in the seat sensor pad

U0170.t: Lost Communication With Restraint System Sensor "A"
U0170.m: The other computers in the car stopped hearing from an airbag system sensor. Features that depend on it can stop working, and several warning lights often come on together.
c: Wiring or connector fault on the data network
Power or ground problem at an airbag system sensor

P0443.t: Evaporative Emission System Purge Control Valve Circuit
P0443.m: The purge valve circuit has an electrical fault.

P0464.t: Fuel Level Sensor A Circuit Intermittent
P0464.m: The fuel level signal drops out now and then.

B1764.m: The airbag system found a fault in the front passenger seat occupant detection pad. The airbag light comes on and the passenger airbag may not be set correctly.
c: Failed passenger seat occupant detection sensor pad
Wiring or connector fault to the pad
Liquid or electronics on the seat cushion (temporary)

P0326.m: The knock sensor signal is outside its expected range.

B141C.t: Second-Row Right Inflatable Seat Belt Circuit Fault
B141C.m: The airbag computer found a problem in the wiring to the right (passenger-side) second-row inflatable seat belt, so it turns on the airbag warning light. That belt's airbag may not deploy in a crash until it is fixed.
c: Worn or broken wires in the second-row seat harness (often from folding the seat)
Damaged connector at the base of the right second-row seat

P07E6.m: The computer commanded the transmission out of Park but sensed it never left Park (the park lock stayed engaged). The vehicle may refuse to move or shift out of Park.
c: Faulty electronic park lock actuator or park pawl motor
Park position sensor or wiring fault
Valve body or internal park mechanism problem

P0411.t: Secondary Air Injection System Incorrect Flow Detected
P0411.m: The secondary air system isn't moving the right amount of air.

P0123.t: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor A Circuit High
P0123.m: The throttle position signal is too high.

P0122.t: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor A Circuit Low
P0122.m: The throttle position signal is too low.

B1346.m: The airbag computer reads too much resistance in the first-stage circuit of the steering wheel airbag. The airbag light stays on and the driver airbag may not deploy.
c: Worn or broken clock spring behind the steering wheel
Loose or corroded driver airbag connector

U0404.t: Invalid Data Received From Gear Shift Control Module "A"
U0404.m: Another computer in the car received data from the gear shift module that did not make sense.
c: A fault inside the gear shift module

P2402.t: Evaporative Emission System Leak Detection Pump Control Circuit High
P2402.m: The EVAP leak test pump circuit reads too high.

C121C.m: The ABS/stability computer asked the engine computer to cut power (for traction or stability control) and the request was refused. Stability/traction lights may come on; owners also report hesitation or stalling, usually because of an underlying engine fault or software mismatch.
c: Engine computer (PCM) software that conflicts with ABS module software
Another engine fault stopping the PCM from accepting torque requests
Can set during very heavy load driving

P0088.m: Fuel pressure is higher than the computer wants.

P26B7.t: Engine Coolant Bypass Valve C Control Circuit/Open
P26B7.m: The computer found a broken (open) circuit to coolant bypass valve C, so it can't control that valve. The engine may warm slowly, run at an unstable temperature or, in bad cases, overheat.
c: Broken wire or loose connector at the valve

P0E15.t: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Coolant Heater A Control Performance
P0E15.m: On a plug-in hybrid or EV, the electric heater that warms the coolant (and battery) isn't doing what the computer commands. Cabin heat or battery warming can suffer, and some vehicles may have start or charging trouble in the cold.
c: Wiring, connector or communication (LIN) fault to the heater

B2960.t: Security System Sensor Data Incorrect but Valid
B2960.m: The anti-theft (Passlock) system got an ignition key/lock signal it didn't expect, so it blocks starting. The car may not crank or may start and stall, and the security light flashes.
c: Worn ignition switch / lock cylinder Passlock sensor contact
Poor connection at the body control module
Wiring fault in the Passlock sensor circuit

P0352.m: The computer sees an electrical fault in ignition coil B (usually the coil for cylinder 2). That cylinder may misfire. If the check engine light flashes, ease off and get it checked right away.
c: Worn spark plug overloading the coil

P0505.m: The idle control isn't holding the right idle speed.
c: Dirty throttle body or IAC valve

B1378.t: Side Airbag Front Driver Resistance Too High
B1378.m: The airbag computer reads too much resistance in the circuit of the driver front seat side airbag. The airbag light comes on and that side airbag may not deploy.
c: Loose or high-resistance side airbag connector under the driver seat

P0351.m: The computer sees an electrical fault in ignition coil A (usually the coil for cylinder 1). That cylinder may misfire. If the check engine light flashes, ease off and get it checked right away.
c: Worn spark plug overloading the coil

P0449.t: Evaporative Emission System Vent Valve/Solenoid Circuit
P0449.m: The EVAP vent valve circuit has an electrical fault.

P0418.t: Secondary Air Injection System Control A Circuit
P0418.m: The relay or circuit that runs the secondary air pump has a fault.

U0103.t: Lost Communication With Gear Shift Module
U0103.m: The other computers in the car stopped hearing from the gear shift module. Features that depend on it can stop working, and several warning lights often come on together.
c: Wiring or connector fault on the data network
Power or ground problem at the gear shift module

P07AE.t: Transmission Friction Element G Performance/Stuck Off
P07AE.m: In an automatic transmission, clutch/friction element G isn't gripping when it should (slipping or not applying). Drivers notice slipping, flares, harsh or missed shifts.
c: Worn clutch pack or leaking seals
Sticking valve or solenoid in the valve body

P069E.t: Fuel Pump Control Module Requested MIL Illumination
P069E.m: The fuel pump control module found its own fault and turned on the check engine light.

C1B00.m: The power steering (or active steering) module got a steering angle reading that is erratic or does not agree with its other sensors. Depending on the sub-code, power assist may be cut to manual steering, or stability and lane features are limited, with a warning on the dash.
c: Faulty steering angle sensor or electric steering gear
Steering wheel or column misaligned after service
Wiring or connector fault to the sensor

B1325.m: A control module saw its main power supply voltage go too low or too high. It usually points to a battery, charging or ground problem, and can come with flickering electronics, warning lights or a no-start.
c: Corroded battery terminals or bad ground

P0627.m: The fuel pump control circuit is open. The engine may not start or may stall.
c: Failed fuel pump relay or module

P0339.t: Crankshaft Position Sensor A Circuit Intermittent
P0339.m: The crankshaft position signal drops out now and then, which can cause sudden stalling.

B0001.m: The airbag computer found a problem in the circuit to the first-stage inflator of the steering wheel airbag (open, high or low resistance, or shorted). The airbag light comes on and the driver airbag may not deploy.
c: Worn or damaged clock spring (cable reel)
Corroded or damaged airbag connector pins

P0481.m: The computer commanded the second radiator cooling fan (or its relay) but the circuit didn't respond as expected, so that fan may not run. The engine can run hot in traffic or at idle, and A/C may cool poorly.
c: Failed fan relay or fan control module
Open or shorted wiring, blown fuse or bad connector

P20BA.t: Reductant Heater A Control Circuit Performance
P20BA.m: On a diesel with DEF (diesel exhaust fluid), the heater that keeps the DEF from freezing isn't performing as commanded. The emissions system can be disabled, and after a while the truck may limit speed or power.
c: Failed DEF tank heater (often part of the tank/pump assembly)
Damaged wiring or connector in the heater circuit

P2681.t: Engine Coolant Bypass Valve A Control Circuit/Open
P2681.m: The computer found a broken (open) circuit to coolant bypass valve A, so it can't control coolant flow through that valve. Warm-up, heater output and engine temperature can be affected.
c: Blown fuse in the valve circuit

P06DA.m: The circuit that switches the oil pump between pressures is open.

U0422.t: Invalid Data Received From Body Control Module
U0422.m: Another computer in the car received data from the body control module that did not make sense.
c: A fault inside the body control module

P0325.m: The knock sensor signal is missing or out of range, so the computer plays it safe and the engine may feel sluggish.

P0750.m: Shift solenoid A isn't working as commanded, so the transmission may skip gears, shift harshly or stay in one gear.

P0022.t: A Camshaft Position Timing Over-Retarded (Intake, Bank 2)
P0022.m: The variable valve timing for the intake camshaft on bank 2 isn't where the computer asked it to be. The engine can idle rough, lose power or use more fuel. Low or dirty oil is a common trigger, because oil pressure moves the timing.
c: Low, old or wrong-grade engine oil

P0307.m: Cylinder 7 is not firing properly, so the engine runs rough and loses some power. A flashing check engine light means the misfire is serious enough to damage the catalytic converter, so slow down and get it checked right away.
c: Spark plug or ignition coil on cylinder 7

P0345.m: The computer can't read the bank 2 camshaft position sensor.

P0457.t: Evaporative Emission System Leak Detected (Fuel Cap Loose/Off)
P0457.m: The computer thinks the gas cap is loose or missing.
c: Gas cap loose, missing or worn

P2015.t: Intake Manifold Runner Position Sensor/Switch Circuit Range/Performance (Bank 1)
P2015.m: The intake runner position reading doesn't make sense.

C0561.m: This is an information code: the brake/stability computer turned off stability and traction control because it saw a problem somewhere else. A 'Service StabiliTrak' or traction warning shows; the real cause is in another stored code.
c: Another fault such as a wheel speed sensor, throttle or engine code
Invalid or missing data from another module on the network

B1861.t: Open in Driver Side Knee Airbag Squib Circuit
B1861.m: The airbag computer found a broken circuit to the driver's knee airbag under the dashboard. The airbag light stays on and the knee airbag may not deploy in a crash.
c: Damaged wire in the instrument panel harness to the knee airbag
Faulty knee airbag or airbag sensor module

P0AA6.t: Hybrid Battery Voltage System Isolation Fault
P0AA6.m: High voltage is leaking somewhere it shouldn't. This is a safety fault: get it checked by a hybrid-trained shop.

B0022.m: The airbag computer sees a wiring or resistance fault in one of the circuits that fire an airbag or seat-belt tensioner. The airbag light comes on and that part may not deploy.
c: Loose, corroded or damaged airbag connector
Wiring rubbed or pinched (often under a seat or in the steering column)
Aftermarket phone/USB charger interference on some GM trucks

U1110.m: A module stopped receiving the vehicle speed message it expects over the vehicle network. Speed-based features (speedometer, cruise, shifting, stability) can act up and warning lights may come on.
c: Wheel speed or ABS module fault upstream
Network (CAN bus) wiring or connector problem
Module that sends the speed signal not communicating

P2097.t: Post Catalyst Fuel Trim System Too Rich (Bank 1)
P2097.m: After the catalytic converter, the exhaust reads too rich for too long.

P1603.m: The engine computer recorded that the engine stalled by itself while the key/power was still on. It is a record of a stall, not proof that one part has failed.
c: Fuel delivery problem (weak pump, low fuel)
Carbon buildup or air intake problems causing a rough idle
Engine computer software or wet/corroded engine computer connectors

P2635.m: The fuel pump isn't delivering enough fuel. Hesitation and stalling can follow.

P1921.m: A module reported a problem with the gear-selector (PRNDL) position signal it receives. Drivers may see shifting problems, a wrong gear display, or starting issues.
c: Wiring or connector problem on the range signal circuit
Communication problem between the transmission and engine modules

P000A.m: The bank 1 intake cam timing changes slower than commanded.

P0A78.m: On a hybrid or EV, the inverter that powers the main electric drive motor reported a fault (for example overheating or a power transistor problem). The hybrid system warning comes on and the car may lose power or shut down drive.
c: Failed inverter/power module (often replaced as an assembly)

P219F.m: Cylinder 4 is getting a different air-fuel mix than the other cylinders.

P2615.t: Camshaft Position Signal Output Circuit Low
P2615.m: The camshaft signal the engine computer sends to other modules reads low.

P1811.m: The transmission computer saw shifts taking too long and has run out of room to adjust for it. It raises line pressure to protect the clutches, so shifts become harsh or firm.
c: Transmission computer needing an updated calibration (4T65 bulletin)
Worn clutches or a failing pressure control solenoid

P0735.m: Fifth gear isn't matching the expected engine-to-wheel speed, which usually means slipping in that gear.

C1513.m: The stability/ABS computer sees a brake pedal switch signal that does not make sense, for example the brake lights stay on when the pedal is released. The ESC or traction light comes on and the brake lights may stay lit.
c: Worn or missing brake pedal stopper pad
Faulty or mis-adjusted brake light switch

C0460.m: The computer that uses the steering wheel angle (power steering or stability control) found the angle reading is wrong or off-center. Drivers may see a Service ESC / Steering Assist Reduced message, stability control acting at odd times, or poor steering return.
c: Steering angle sensor not centered/calibrated after an alignment or repair
Power steering or brake module software needing an update
Internal fault in the electric steering gear (some 2020-21 GM SUVs)

P1121.t: Coolant Flow Control Valve Position Sensor Circuit Stuck
P1121.m: On the 2nd-gen Prius, the engine computer saw the coolant valve for the hot-coolant storage tank not moving when told to. The check engine light comes on; warm-up and heater performance can suffer.
c: Clogged cooling passages or dirty coolant
Faulty valve position sensor or engine computer

P1500.m: The engine computer saw a problem with the vehicle speed signal. The speedometer, cruise control or shifting may act up, and the check engine light may come on.
c: Damaged wiring or connector to the speed sensor
Problem in the module that supplies the speed signal

P0131.t: O2 Sensor Circuit Low Voltage (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
P0131.m: The upstream O2 sensor reads too low.

P0638.m: The electronic throttle isn't moving the way it's commanded. The car may go into reduced power.

P2401.t: Evaporative Emission System Leak Detection Pump Control Circuit Low
P2401.m: The EVAP leak test pump circuit reads too low.

P0192.t: Fuel Rail Pressure Sensor A Circuit Low
P0192.m: The fuel pressure sensor signal is too low.

P0353.m: The computer sees an electrical fault in ignition coil C (usually the coil for cylinder 3). That cylinder may misfire. If the check engine light flashes, ease off and get it checked right away.
c: Worn spark plug overloading the coil

C0242.m: The engine computer told the brake module it can't carry out traction control (it can't cut engine power when asked). Traction control turns off and its warning light comes on; the root cause is usually an engine fault.
c: Engine fault stored in the ECM/PCM (throttle body, sensor or misfire)
Communication problem between the engine and brake modules
Loose pin in the transmission/engine connector (Cadillac case)

P0521.t: Engine Oil Pressure Sensor/Switch A Range/Performance
P0521.m: The oil pressure reading doesn't make sense. Check the oil level first.

U1120.m: A module stopped receiving the wheel distance (wheel rotation) message it expects over the vehicle network. Odometer, speed-based features and stability systems may misbehave and warning lights can come on.
c: ABS module or wheel speed sensor fault upstream
Network (CAN bus) wiring or connector problem

U2011.m: On Ford electric power steering, the steering module found a fault with the assist motor's electronics or its signals. Power assist is removed, so steering turns heavy and a warning appears.
c: Failed power steering assist motor or its electronics
Internal fault in the electric steering gear

P0887.t: TCM Power Relay Control Circuit High
P0887.m: The computer sees too-high voltage in the circuit that switches the transmission control module's power relay. The transmission may shift erratically or go into limp mode, and traction control or ABS can switch off.
c: Wiring short to power in the relay control circuit

P2172.t: Throttle Actuator Control System - High Airflow Detected (Sudden)
P2172.m: The computer saw a sudden, unexpected jump in airflow.

P0965.t: Pressure Control Solenoid B Control Circuit Range/Performance
P0965.m: The circuit for transmission pressure solenoid B isn't performing as expected.

P0556.t: Brake Booster Pressure Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
P0556.m: The brake booster vacuum reading doesn't make sense. Brakes may feel harder to press.

P023F.m: The computer watches a feedback wire on the fuel pump's power feed and found it reading wrong when the pump should be off. The fuel pump may keep running with the key off, which can drain the battery.
c: Stuck or faulty fuel pump relay
Wiring short to voltage in the pump supply or feedback circuit
Fuel pump control module or engine computer driver fault

P0219.m: The engine went past its safe RPM.
c: Missed shift or downshift at speed

P0452.t: Evaporative Emission System Pressure Sensor/Switch Low
P0452.m: The fuel tank pressure sensor reads too low.

P0884.m: The transmission computer's power supply drops out now and then.

B0116.t: Open in Side Squib LH Circuit
B0116.m: The airbag computer found a broken circuit to the left-side (driver side) seat airbag igniter. The airbag light stays on and that side airbag may not deploy in a crash.
c: Damaged or loose floor wiring harness / connector under the left front seat

B0092.m: On GM vehicles the passenger seat sensing system isn't working correctly, so the airbag computer can't tell if someone is in the seat. The airbag light comes on and the passenger airbag may be turned off.
c: Failed passenger seat sensor/module or cushion
Broken wires or loose connector under the passenger seat

P0175.m: Bank 2 is getting too much fuel.

P0354.m: The computer sees an electrical fault in ignition coil D (usually the coil for cylinder 4). That cylinder may misfire. If the check engine light flashes, ease off and get it checked right away.
c: Worn spark plug overloading the coil

P2419.t: Evaporative Emission System Switching Valve Control Circuit Low
P2419.m: The computer saw low voltage in the circuit for the EVAP leak-check switching valve, so the fuel vapor leak test can't run. There are usually no driving symptoms, just the check engine light.
c: Faulty leak detection pump / canister pump module (most common)
Wiring short to ground or bad connector

P0451.t: Evaporative Emission System Pressure Sensor/Switch Range/Performance
P0451.m: The fuel tank pressure reading doesn't make sense.

P0461.t: Fuel Level Sensor A Circuit Range/Performance
P0461.m: The fuel level reading doesn't make sense, so the gauge may jump around.

P0308.m: Cylinder 8 is not firing properly, so the engine runs rough and loses some power. A flashing check engine light means the misfire is serious enough to damage the catalytic converter, so slow down and get it checked right away.
c: Spark plug or ignition coil on cylinder 8

P00AF.t: Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Control A Module Performance
P00AF.m: The module or actuator that controls turbo boost (often the electronic actuator on a variable-geometry turbo) isn't working as expected. Boost can be wrong, so the engine may lose power and go into a reduced-power mode.
c: Failed electronic turbo actuator / boost control module
Sticking turbo vanes from soot buildup

P0524.m: Oil pressure is too low. Stop the engine as soon as it's safe: low oil pressure can destroy an engine quickly.
c: Low oil level or a leak

P20EE.t: SCR NOx Catalyst Efficiency Below Threshold Bank 1
P20EE.m: On a diesel, the SCR catalyst that uses DEF to cut NOx isn't cleaning the exhaust as well as it should. Often the only sign is the warning light, but the truck may later limit speed or power.
c: Clogged or faulty DEF injector/doser or pump
Faulty NOx or exhaust temperature sensor

U0002.t: High Speed CAN Communication Bus Performance
U0002.m: The main data network isn't performing as expected.

B1481.m: The airbag computer reads too much resistance in the second-stage circuit of the steering wheel airbag. The airbag light stays on and the driver airbag may not work properly.
c: Loose or corroded driver airbag connector

P0A94.m: The hybrid system's voltage converter isn't performing as expected.

P0751.m: Shift solenoid A isn't working as commanded, so the transmission may skip gears, shift harshly or stay in one gear.

P2832.t: Shift Fork A Position Circuit Range/Performance
P2832.m: In an automated manual or dual-clutch transmission, the sensor reading for shift fork A is out of the expected range, so the computer can't be sure which gear is selected. Expect hesitation, harsh or missed shifts, or the car refusing to go into some gears.
c: Failing transmission control module (has its own position sensors on Ford DPS6)
Worn or broken internal shift drum/fork stop

P0113.t: Intake Air Temperature Sensor 1 Circuit High
P0113.m: The intake air temperature sensor reads as an open circuit (very cold).

P2701.t: Transmission Friction Element B Apply Time Range/Performance
P2701.m: Clutch pack B inside the transmission takes too long (or too little time) to engage, so shifts can slip or flare.

P2764.t: Torque Converter Clutch Pressure Control Solenoid Control Circuit Low
P2764.m: The torque converter clutch pressure solenoid circuit reads too low.

P228D.t: Fuel Pressure Regulator 1 Exceeded Control Limits - Pressure Too High
P228D.m: The fuel pressure regulator can't keep pressure down.

B0028.t: Right Side Seat Air Bag Squib 1 Circuit Open
B0028.m: The airbag computer sees an open circuit to the right (passenger) front seat side airbag. The airbag light comes on and that side airbag may not deploy.
c: Poor connection in the seat-to-body connector under the seat

P26CB.m: The electric water pump isn't running or isn't pumping at the speed the computer commands. Coolant may not circulate properly, so the engine can overheat.
c: Failed electric water pump (common on newer Toyota 2.5L engines)
Wiring, relay or fuse problem in the pump circuit
Low coolant or air trapped in the system

P0405.t: Exhaust Gas Recirculation Sensor A Circuit Low
P0405.m: The EGR position sensor reads too low.

C0040.t: Right Front Wheel Speed Sensor Circuit
C0040.m: The ABS module sees a bad or missing signal from the right front wheel speed sensor. ABS, traction and stability lights come on and those systems are switched off.
c: Failed right front wheel speed sensor
Damaged or corroded sensor wiring or connector
Damaged or dirty tone ring / hub bearing

P0756.m: Shift solenoid B isn't working as commanded, so the transmission may skip gears, shift harshly or stay in one gear.

P1750.t: A/T Clutch Pressure Control Solenoid Hydraulic Problem
P1750.m: The transmission computer sees that gear clutch pressure is not behaving as commanded, pointing to a mechanical or hydraulic problem in the automatic transmission. Shifts can slip, flare or feel harsh, and the check engine light comes on.
c: Clogged screens or sticking clutch pressure control (linear) solenoids
Low, old or dirty transmission fluid
Valve body or internal transmission wear

P0141.m: The downstream O2 sensor's heater isn't working.

P0758.m: Shift solenoid B isn't working as commanded, so the transmission may skip gears, shift harshly or stay in one gear.

P0068.m: The air flow, manifold pressure and throttle readings don't agree with each other. The car may go into reduced power.

C1235.t: Right Rear Wheel Speed Sensor Signal Missing
C1235.m: The ABS module is not getting a signal from the right rear wheel speed sensor. The ABS and traction control lights come on and those systems are switched off; normal brakes still work.
c: Failed right rear wheel speed sensor
Corroded or broken wiring between the ABS module and the sensor
Damaged tone ring or wrong sensor gap

P0137.t: O2 Sensor Circuit Low Voltage (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
P0137.m: The downstream O2 sensor reads too low.

P043E.t: Evaporative Emission System Leak Detection Reference Orifice Low Flow
P043E.m: The EVAP leak test's reference port reads low flow.

P0402.t: Exhaust Gas Recirculation A Flow Excessive Detected
P0402.m: Too much exhaust gas is going back into the engine, which can cause a rough idle or stalling.

B1701.t: Driver Seat Belt Buckle Pretensioner Resistance High
B1701.m: The airbag computer reads too much resistance in the driver seat belt buckle pretensioner circuit. The airbag light comes on.
c: Loose or poorly mating connector under the driver seat
Worn or faulty driver seat belt buckle assembly

B1054.t: Driver Air Bag Stage 2 Circuit Open
B1054.m: The airbag computer sees an open circuit in the second-stage circuit of the steering wheel airbag. The airbag light stays on and the driver airbag may not work properly.
c: Worn or broken spiral cable (clock spring)
Damaged driver airbag wiring or connector

P0944.t: Hydraulic Pressure Unit Loss of Pressure
P0944.m: The transmission's hydraulic unit is losing pressure.

P0685.m: The relay that powers the engine computer has a circuit fault.

P0222.t: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor B Circuit Low
P0222.m: The second throttle position signal is too low.

C0800.m: A chassis control module saw its supply voltage go out of range. On GM trucks it shows up with low power steering assist, stalling, blank gauges/radio and many other network codes.
c: Poor body control module ground (G218 on 2014-16 GM full-size trucks/SUVs)
Shorted battery cable at the starter

P2445.t: Secondary Air Injection System Pump Stuck Off (Bank 1)
P2445.m: The secondary air pump isn't running when commanded.

C1130.m: The ABS/stability computer is not getting a valid signal from the engine computer. ABS/VDC/traction lights can come on and features like intelligent cruise and emergency braking may switch off.
c: An engine fault that already set its own P-code
Engine computer signal or CAN message missing
Wiring or network fault between the engine and ABS computers

P0471.t: Exhaust Pressure Sensor A Circuit Range/Performance
P0471.m: The exhaust pressure sensor's reading doesn't match what the computer expects (for example compared with intake and air pressure at key-on). Power can drop and diesel particulate filter cleaning may not run.
c: Blocked or cracked tube between the exhaust and the sensor
Air intake, EGR or charge-air leaks

U1412.m: A module received a vehicle speed signal over the network that doesn't make sense. Speedometer, cruise, shifting or stability features can act up and warning lights may come on.
c: Faulty wheel speed sensor or ABS module sending bad speed data
Wrong tire size or module configuration

C056D.m: A chassis computer (power steering, brake/ABS or park brake) found a fault inside itself or in a part it directly drives. Depending on the vehicle you see Service Power Steering with heavy steering, or a Service Parking Brake message with park-brake and ABS lights.
c: Faulty power steering assist motor (2016-2018 Colorado/Canyon)
High resistance in the electric park brake actuator or its wiring (many 2017-2022 GM SUVs/trucks)

B101D.m: The passenger presence (seat sensing) module reports an internal hardware fault. The airbag warning message comes on and the passenger airbag may be turned off.
c: Passenger seat sensor mat loose or disengaged

C1A16.m: The front radar sensor in the bumper cannot see clearly, so intelligent cruise control and automatic emergency braking switch off and a 'front radar obstruction' or 'front sensor blocked' message shows.
c: Dirt, snow, ice or a stain on the radar cover
Something mounted in front of the sensor (plate frame, bra, damage)

U0146.m: The other computers in the car stopped hearing from the gateway module. Features that depend on it can stop working, and several warning lights often come on together.
c: Wiring or connector fault on the data network
Power or ground problem at the gateway module

P2872.m: In a dual-clutch or automated manual transmission, clutch A stays engaged when the computer wants it released. The car can lurch, stall when stopping, shudder or refuse to shift.
c: Worn or contaminated clutch (fluid leak onto it)
Faulty clutch A actuator or release mechanism

P2704.t: Transmission Friction Element E Apply Time Range/Performance
P2704.m: Clutch pack E inside the transmission takes too long (or too little time) to engage, so shifts can slip or flare.

P07A5.t: Transmission Friction Element B Stuck On
P07A5.m: In an automatic transmission, clutch/friction element B stays applied when the computer wants it released. Shifts can be harsh or binding, and the transmission may go into limp mode.
c: Low, old or contaminated transmission fluid
Stuck valve or solenoid in the valve body
Worn or damaged internal clutch parts

U2603.t: Lost Communication With Battery Interface Module 1
U2603.m: The Volt's main battery computer lost contact with one of the small modules that watch the high-voltage battery cells. The check engine light comes on and the car may not start.
c: Internal fault in the battery energy control module
Wiring to the battery interface modules

C0631.m: On some AWD Explorers and Aviators, the computer found a problem with the front axle disconnect unit that connects and disconnects the front wheels. The wrench (powertrain) light comes on and AWD may not work properly.
c: Faulty front axle disconnect actuator / intermediate shaft
Wiring or connector problem at the disconnect actuator

P0196.m: The oil temperature reading doesn't make sense.

P0421.t: Warm Up Catalyst Efficiency Below Threshold (Bank 1)
P0421.m: The small warm-up catalytic converter on bank 1 isn't working as well as it should.

P0135.m: The upstream O2 sensor's heater isn't working.

C1231.m: The stability control computer got a bad or uncalibrated signal from the sensor that reads which way the steering wheel is turned. VSC/TRAC lights come on and stability control may act wrongly or switch off.
c: Steering angle sensor not calibrated (center point not stored)
Faulty steering angle sensor or its wiring
Skid control computer software (2003 Sequoia recall/bulletin)

P0410.m: The system that pumps air into the exhaust during cold starts has a fault.

P0701.m: The transmission control system isn't performing as expected.

C1201.m: The stability control system turned off because the engine computer reported its own fault. VSC/TRAC lights come on along with the check engine light; fix the engine code first.
c: Any stored engine fault (check engine light code)
Wiring between the engine and skid control computers

P2293.m: The second fuel pressure regulator isn't holding the right pressure.

P0240.t: Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Sensor B Circuit Range/Performance
P0240.m: The second boost pressure sensor's reading doesn't make sense compared with what the computer expects, often showing more boost than commanded. The computer cuts power to protect the engine.
c: Leaking, pinched or cracked boost or vacuum hoses
Faulty wastegate control solenoid or stuck wastegate

P051B.m: The crankcase pressure reading doesn't make sense.

P2715.t: Pressure Control Solenoid D Stuck On
P2715.m: Transmission pressure solenoid D is stuck on.

P2118.t: Throttle Actuator Control Motor Current Range/Performance
P2118.m: The throttle motor is drawing an unexpected current.

P000B.m: The bank 1 exhaust cam timing changes slower than commanded.

P0138.t: O2 Sensor Circuit High Voltage (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
P0138.m: The downstream O2 sensor reads too high.

P0AC4.t: Hybrid/EV Powertrain Control Module Requested MIL Illumination
