P0AC4.m: The hybrid/EV control module found a fault of its own and asked the engine computer to turn on the check engine light. The real problem is in another code stored in the hybrid system, which can range from minor to serious.
c: A fault stored in the hybrid/EV module (battery, cooling, motor, charging)
High-voltage battery temperature or voltage problem
Battery cooling fan, sensor or coolant problem

U0111.t: Lost Communication With Battery Energy Control Module "A"
U0111.m: The other computers in the car stopped hearing from the battery energy control module. Features that depend on it can stop working, and several warning lights often come on together.
c: Wiring or connector fault on the data network
Power or ground problem at the battery energy control module

P287B.t: Shift Fork A Calibration Not Learned
P287B.m: The transmission computer doesn't have a valid learned position for shift fork A, usually after a repair or module replacement, or because the learn keeps failing. Shifting can be rough or some gears may not engage.
c: Shift fork learn/adaptation not run after a repair or module swap
Learn fails because of a faulty transmission control module
Worn internal shift parts (e.g. shift drum stop)

P0597.m: The electrically heated thermostat circuit is open.

P0236.m: The boost pressure reading doesn't make sense.

P2173.t: Throttle Actuator Control System - High Airflow Detected (Slow)
P2173.m: The computer saw airflow creeping higher than expected.

U2622.t: Lost Communication With Battery Interface Module 10
U2622.m: The Volt's main battery computer lost contact with battery cell monitoring module 10. The check engine light comes on and the car may not start.
c: Internal fault in the battery energy control module
Wiring to the battery interface modules

U2624.t: Lost Communication With Battery Interface Module 12
U2624.m: The Volt's main battery computer lost contact with battery cell monitoring module 12. The check engine light comes on and the car may not start.
c: Internal fault in the battery energy control module
Wiring to the battery interface modules

C0063.m: The vehicle stability system on a Can-Am Spyder or Ryker got a bad signal from the sensor that measures how fast the vehicle is turning. Stability and traction control can shut off and the vehicle may go into limp mode.
c: Steering angle sensor zero point not learned or lost
Excess play in the front steering/suspension parts
Wiring or connector problem, or low battery voltage

P076F.m: In 7th gear, the transmission's input and output speeds don't match the ratio 7th gear should give, so it is slipping or not fully in that gear. Drivers notice slipping, flares, or delayed or missing 7th-gear shifts.
c: Worn clutch pack or internal leak
Faulty shift solenoid or valve body problem

P061A.m: The engine computer's torque check found a mismatch.

P032F.m: On a hybrid or mild-hybrid, the computer decided the gas engine is making less torque than it should for the commands it's getting. The vehicle may feel down on power, idle roughly or rely more on the electric side.
c: Misfire, low compression or other engine mechanical problem
Fuel delivery problem (weak pump, clogged injectors)
Air intake leak or faulty airflow/pressure sensor

P2732.t: Pressure Control Solenoid F Performance/Stuck Off
P2732.m: Transmission pressure control solenoid F isn't working right or is stuck off, so hydraulic pressure for some shifts is wrong. Expect slipping, harsh or late shifts, or limp mode.
c: Dirty or low transmission fluid, clogged filter
Valve body problem or restricted fluid passages

P0770.m: Shift solenoid E isn't working as commanded, so the transmission may skip gears, shift harshly or stay in one gear.

P0605.t: Internal Control Module Read Only Memory (ROM) Error
P0605.m: The engine computer found an error in its stored programming.

P0775.m: Transmission pressure solenoid B has a fault.

P0745.m: The main transmission pressure solenoid has a fault. Shifts may be harsh or soft.

P0406.t: Exhaust Gas Recirculation Sensor A Circuit High
P0406.m: The EGR position sensor reads too high.

P0752.m: Shift solenoid A isn't working as commanded, so the transmission may skip gears, shift harshly or stay in one gear.

P2646.t: A Rocker Arm Actuator System Performance or Stuck Off (Bank 1)
P2646.m: The variable valve lift system on bank 1 isn't switching as commanded.
c: Failed rocker arm oil control solenoid

P043F.t: Evaporative Emission System Leak Detection Reference Orifice High Flow
P043F.m: The EVAP leak test's reference port reads high flow.

P2002.t: Diesel Particulate Filter Efficiency Below Threshold (Bank 1)
P2002.m: The diesel particulate filter isn't trapping soot as it should.

P060A.t: Internal Control Module Monitoring Processor Performance
P060A.m: The engine computer's backup processor found a problem.

P0A3F.t: Drive Motor A Position Sensor Circuit
P0A3F.m: On a hybrid or EV, the circuit for the sensor that tracks the electric drive motor's rotor position has a fault. The hybrid system warning comes on and the car may lose power or refuse to drive.
c: Open, shorted or corroded wiring or connector
Inverter or hybrid control module fault

U0141.t: Lost Communication With Body Control Module "A"
U0141.m: The other computers in the car stopped hearing from body control module A. Features that depend on it can stop working, and several warning lights often come on together.
c: Wiring or connector fault on the data network
Power or ground problem at body control module A

P2195.t: O2 Sensor Signal Biased/Stuck Lean (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
P2195.m: The upstream O2 sensor keeps reading lean.

P2176.t: Throttle Actuator Control System - Idle Position Not Learned
P2176.m: The computer hasn't learned the throttle's closed position, often after battery work or cleaning.

P0504.m: The two brake pedal switch signals disagree. Cruise control may stop working and brake lights may act up.

P0324.m: The knock detection system found a fault, so the computer may pull timing and the engine feels weaker.

P2837.t: Shift Fork B Position Circuit Range/Performance
P2837.m: In an automated manual or dual-clutch transmission, the sensor reading for shift fork B is out of the expected range, so the computer can't confirm the gear position. Expect harsh or missed shifts, or some gears not engaging.
c: Failing transmission control module (has its own position sensors on Ford DPS6)
Worn or broken internal shift drum/fork stop

P2583.t: Cruise Control Front Distance Range Sensor Single Sensor or Center
P2583.m: The front radar (or single center distance sensor) used by adaptive cruise control reported a fault or an implausible reading. Adaptive cruise, and often collision-warning or auto-braking features, turn off until it's fixed.
c: Dirt, snow or ice covering the radar sensor
Radar knocked out of alignment (minor bump, bumper repair)

P0366.m: The second cam sensor signal on bank 1 doesn't look right.

P068A.t: ECM/PCM Power Relay De-Energized - Too Early
P068A.m: The engine computer lost power sooner than expected after shut-off.

P20B9.m: On a diesel with DEF, the computer found a broken (open) circuit to the heater that keeps the DEF from freezing. The emissions system may be disabled and the truck may eventually limit speed or power.
c: Failed DEF heater (often part of the tank/pump assembly)
Broken wire or bad connector in the heater circuit
Blown fuse or relay in the heater circuit

P0090.m: The circuit that controls fuel pressure has an electrical fault.

P0002.t: Fuel Volume Regulator Control Circuit Range/Performance
P0002.m: The circuit for the valve that regulates how much fuel the high-pressure pump delivers is reading out of range. Fuel pressure can be wrong, causing hard starts, no-start, stalling or reduced power.
c: Wiring short, open or corroded connector

P06DE.t: Engine Oil Pressure Control Circuit Stuck On
P06DE.m: The variable oil pump is stuck in one pressure mode.

P083B.t: Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch G Circuit Range/Performance
P083B.m: The transmission fluid pressure sensor or switch 'G' is reporting values the computer doesn't expect. Shift quality changes, and the transmission may go into limp mode (starting in 2nd or 3rd gear).
c: Open or shorted wiring in the sensor circuit

P018B.t: Fuel Pressure Sensor B Circuit Range/Performance
P018B.m: The second fuel pressure sensor's reading doesn't make sense to the computer. The engine may be hard to start, not start, or run poorly.
c: Real fuel delivery problem (weak pump, clogged filter)

P084A.t: Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch H Circuit
P084A.m: The circuit for transmission fluid pressure sensor or switch 'H' has an electrical fault. Shift quality changes and the transmission may go into limp mode.
c: Open or short in the sensor wiring
Internal transmission problem affecting the sensor

P287A.m: In a dual-clutch or automated manual transmission, clutch B stays engaged when the computer wants it released. The car can lurch, shudder, stall when stopping or refuse to shift.
c: Worn or contaminated clutch (fluid leak onto it)
Faulty clutch B actuator or release mechanism

P2682.t: Engine Coolant Bypass Valve A Control Circuit Low
P2682.m: The computer sees too-low voltage (often a short to ground) in the circuit that controls coolant bypass valve A. The engine may warm slowly, run at the wrong temperature or give weak heat.
c: Failed coolant control valve (Subaru thermo control valve)
Coolant vapor getting into the valve's electronics
Wiring short to ground or damaged connector

P26A5.t: Engine Coolant Bypass Valve A Position Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
P26A5.m: The position sensor inside coolant bypass valve A is giving readings the computer doesn't expect. Engine temperature control can be off, with slow warm-up or weak heat.
c: Failed coolant control valve or its built-in position sensor
Coolant vapor or leaks damaging the sensor

P2703.t: Transmission Friction Element D Apply Time Range/Performance
P2703.m: Clutch pack D inside the transmission takes too long (or too little time) to engage, so shifts can slip or flare.

P0460.m: The fuel gauge sender has an electrical fault, so the gauge may be wrong.

P0355.m: The computer sees an electrical fault in ignition coil E (usually the coil for cylinder 5). That cylinder may misfire. If the check engine light flashes, ease off and get it checked right away.
c: Worn spark plug overloading the coil

P0753.m: Shift solenoid A isn't working as commanded, so the transmission may skip gears, shift harshly or stay in one gear.

P2128.t: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch E Circuit High
P2128.m: The second gas pedal position signal reads too high.

U0129.t: Lost Communication With Brake System Control Module
U0129.m: The other computers in the car stopped hearing from the brake system control module. Features that depend on it can stop working, and several warning lights often come on together.
c: Wiring or connector fault on the data network
Power or ground problem at the brake system control module

P0203.m: The fuel injector circuit for cylinder 3 is open or faulty, so that cylinder may get no fuel and misfire.

P2723.t: Pressure Control Solenoid E Performance/Stuck Off
P2723.m: Transmission pressure solenoid E isn't controlling pressure.

P0792.t: Intermediate Shaft Speed Sensor A Circuit Range/Performance
P0792.m: The speed sensor on the transmission's intermediate shaft is giving readings that don't fit what the computer expects. Shifting can become harsh or erratic and the transmission may go into a backup mode.
c: Wiring or connector problem to the sensor

P0403.t: Exhaust Gas Recirculation A Control Circuit
P0403.m: The EGR valve control circuit has an electrical fault.

U0109.t: Lost Communication With Fuel Pump Control Module
U0109.m: The other computers in the car stopped hearing from the fuel pump control module. Features that depend on it can stop working, and several warning lights often come on together.
c: Wiring or connector fault on the data network
Power or ground problem at the fuel pump control module

P0826.t: Up and Down Shift Switch Circuit
P0826.m: The manual shift (+/-) switch circuit has a fault.

P2181.m: The engine isn't holding its normal temperature.

U0428.t: Invalid Data Received From Steering Angle Sensor Module
U0428.m: Another computer in the car received data from the steering angle sensor module that did not make sense.
c: A fault inside the steering angle sensor module

P0445.t: Evaporative Emission System Purge Control Valve Circuit Closed
P0445.m: The purge valve circuit reads shorted.

P2831.m: In an automated manual or dual-clutch transmission, the computer found an electrical fault in the position circuit for shift fork A (the fork for the odd gears on Ford's DPS6). Gears may not engage, shifting can be erratic or the car may not move.
c: Failing transmission control module (houses the position sensors on Ford DPS6)

U0164.t: Lost Communication With HVAC Control Module
U0164.m: The other computers in the car stopped hearing from the climate control module. Features that depend on it can stop working, and several warning lights often come on together.
c: Wiring or connector fault on the data network
Power or ground problem at the climate control module

P2600.m: The electric coolant pump circuit is open, so the engine can overheat.

P2711.m: The transmission dropped out of gear unexpectedly. The car can suddenly lose drive, which is a safety risk.

P2005.t: Intake Manifold Runner Control Stuck Open (Bank 2)
P2005.m: The flaps inside the bank 2 intake manifold are stuck open. Power and smoothness can suffer.
c: Carbon buildup on the runner flaps

P2459.m: The particulate filter is having to clean itself too often.
c: Engine running rich or burning oil

P219D.m: Cylinder 2 is getting a different air-fuel mix than the other cylinders.

P2601.t: Coolant Pump A Control Circuit Range/Performance
P2601.m: The electric coolant pump isn't performing as commanded.

P07E4.m: The transmission computer commanded Park but could not confirm that the transmission actually went into Park. The driver may see a warning to shift to Park or set the parking brake, and the car may not stay put on its own.
c: Fault in the park mechanism or park actuator
Park position sensor or wiring fault

P0133.t: O2 Sensor Circuit Slow Response (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
P0133.m: The upstream O2 sensor reacts too slowly, which hurts fuel control and mileage.

P0140.t: O2 Sensor Circuit No Activity Detected (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
P0140.m: The downstream O2 sensor isn't sending a usable signal.

P2610.t: ECM/PCM Internal Engine Off Timer Performance
P2610.m: The engine computer's internal off-timer isn't working right.

P2121.t: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch D Circuit Range/Performance
P2121.m: One of the gas pedal position signals doesn't make sense.

P2099.t: Post Catalyst Fuel Trim System Too Rich (Bank 2)
P2099.m: After the bank 2 catalytic converter, the exhaust reads too rich.

P0218.m: The transmission is running too hot. Ease off and let it cool; heat wears a transmission fast.

P2443.t: Secondary Air Injection System Switching Valve Stuck Closed (Bank 2)
P2443.m: The valve that lets cold-start air into the bank 2 exhaust is stuck closed.
c: Water or carbon in the valve

P0202.m: The fuel injector circuit for cylinder 2 is open or faulty, so that cylinder may get no fuel and misfire.

P2107.m: The throttle control processor found an internal fault.

P0448.t: Evaporative Emission System Vent Control Circuit Shorted
P0448.m: The EVAP vent valve circuit reads shorted.

P2432.t: Secondary Air Injection System Air Flow/Pressure Sensor Circuit Low (Bank 1)
P2432.m: The secondary air pressure sensor reads too low.

P0108.t: Manifold Absolute Pressure Sensor Circuit High
P0108.m: The MAP sensor signal is too high.

P0760.m: Shift solenoid C isn't working as commanded, so the transmission may skip gears, shift harshly or stay in one gear.

P0031.t: HO2S Heater Control Circuit Low (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
P0031.m: The upstream O2 sensor heater circuit reads too low.

P2017.t: Intake Manifold Runner Position Sensor/Switch Circuit High Bank 1
P2017.m: The engine computer sees a voltage that is too high from the sensor that reports where the intake runner flaps are, on bank 1. The driver may notice the check engine light, a little less power and worse fuel economy.
c: Failed intake runner position sensor or actuator
Wiring or connector fault in the sensor circuit

P0651.m: A 5-volt reference feed to several sensors is faulty, which can trigger a group of other codes.

P0736.m: Reverse isn't matching the expected speed, which usually means slipping in reverse.

P025A.t: Fuel Pump Module A Control Circuit/Open
P025A.m: The engine computer found a break or fault in the circuit it uses to control the fuel pump module. The car may be hard to start, stall, run weakly, or not start at all.
c: Failed fuel pump or fuel pump module
Broken or damaged wiring to the pump module

P0523.t: Engine Oil Pressure Sensor/Switch A Circuit High
P0523.m: The oil pressure sensor reads too high.

P0009.m: The cam and crank timing is drifting out of line on bank 2, often from a stretched timing chain.
c: Faulty cam phaser or VVT solenoid

P0902.m: The automated clutch actuator circuit reads too low.

P0A0A.m: A high-voltage safety interlock is open, so the hybrid system may shut down.

P0600.m: The engine computer has trouble talking to another module.

P0126.t: Insufficient Coolant Temperature for Stable Operation
P0126.m: The engine takes too long to warm up.

P2638.t: Torque Management Feedback Signal A Range/Performance
P2638.m: The engine and transmission computers share a signal about how much torque the engine is making, and that signal does not make sense. Shifts can feel wrong or harsh, and the car may go into a reduced-power mode.
c: Wiring fault between the engine and transmission computers
Engine control module fault or old software

P073E.m: The transmission was asked to go into Reverse but the computer could not confirm that it did. The car may not back up, or the transmission may go into a limited limp mode.
c: Low, dirty or wrong transmission fluid
Blocked hydraulic passage in the transmission

P016F.t: Closed Loop Fuel Pressure Control At Limit - Pressure Too Low
P016F.m: The engine computer has pushed its fuel pressure control as far as it can go and the pressure is still lower than it wants. The engine may lose power, run poorly, or stall.
c: Fuel leak or faulty pressure regulator

P0805.m: The clutch pedal position sensor has a fault.

P2797.m: The extra transmission pump (used by start-stop systems) isn't performing.

P2859.m: The transmission computer saw that the hydraulic pressure on clutch A did not drop the way it should when that clutch was released. Shifts may feel off, and the check engine light comes on.
c: Valve body or hydraulic pressure problem

P0729.m: Sixth gear isn't matching the expected engine-to-wheel speed, so something is slipping.

P059F.t: Active Grille Air Shutter A Performance
P059F.m: The front grille shutters aren't moving as commanded.

P0030.m: The heater in the upstream oxygen sensor has an electrical fault, so the sensor is slow to start working.

P06E9.m: The starter took longer than expected to crank the engine.

U0122.t: Lost Communication With Vehicle Dynamics Control Module
U0122.m: The other computers in the car stopped hearing from the stability control module. Features that depend on it can stop working, and several warning lights often come on together.
c: Wiring or connector fault on the data network
Power or ground problem at the stability control module

P00FF.t: Body Control Module Requested MIL Illumination
P00FF.m: The body control module asked the engine computer to turn on the check engine light because it found a fault of its own. The light itself is the main symptom; the real problem is stored in the body control module.
c: A fault stored in the body control module
Body control module wiring or software issue
Communication problem between the body and engine computers

P26A6.t: Engine Coolant Bypass Valve A Position Sensor Circuit Low
P26A6.m: The engine computer sees a voltage that is too low from the sensor that reports the position of the coolant bypass (coolant control) valve. The check engine light comes on, and engine warm-up or heat control may not work right.
c: Failed coolant bypass valve or its internal position sensor
Broken internal gear in the coolant valve
Wiring short or open in the sensor circuit

P219C.m: Cylinder 1 is getting a different air-fuel mix than the other cylinders.

P01F0.t: Coolant Temperature Relapsed Below Diagnostic Monitoring Temperature
P01F0.m: The engine warmed up enough for its self-tests, then the coolant temperature dropped back below that level. Often the only sign is the check engine light, sometimes with a weak heater.
c: Cooling fan running when it should not

P0761.m: Shift solenoid C isn't working as commanded, so the transmission may skip gears, shift harshly or stay in one gear.

P0742.t: Torque Converter Clutch Solenoid Circuit Stuck On
P0742.m: The torque converter is staying locked when it shouldn't, which can stall the engine when you stop.

P0107.t: Manifold Absolute Pressure Sensor Circuit Low
P0107.m: The MAP sensor signal is too low.

P2637.m: A torque signal between the engine and transmission computers is faulty.

P0845.t: Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch B Circuit
P0845.m: A second transmission fluid pressure switch has a fault.

P0221.m: The second throttle position signal doesn't make sense, so the car may limit power.

P0A93.m: The hybrid inverter isn't being cooled properly. The car can shut down to protect it.

P2444.t: Secondary Air Injection System Pump Stuck On (Bank 1)
P2444.m: The secondary air pump keeps running when it shouldn't.

P0201.m: The fuel injector circuit for cylinder 1 is open or faulty, so that cylinder may get no fuel and misfire.

P0688.t: ECM/PCM Power Relay Sense Circuit Open
P0688.m: The engine computer checks that its main power relay is feeding it voltage, and that check circuit reads open. The car may be slow to start or not start, and some electrical items may stop working.
c: Open or shorted wire between the relay and the computer

P0765.m: Shift solenoid D isn't working as commanded, so the transmission may skip gears, shift harshly or stay in one gear.

P0843.t: Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch A Circuit High
P0843.m: A transmission fluid pressure switch reads too high.

P0766.m: Shift solenoid D isn't working as commanded, so the transmission may skip gears, shift harshly or stay in one gear.

P2562.t: Turbocharger Boost Control Position Sensor Circuit
P2562.m: The engine computer found a problem in the circuit of the sensor that reports where the turbo's boost control (wastegate or vane) is. The engine may feel weak or hesitate, and fuel economy can drop.
c: Lost power or ground at the sensor

P0356.m: The computer sees an electrical fault in ignition coil F (usually the coil for cylinder 6). That cylinder may misfire. If the check engine light flashes, ease off and get it checked right away.
c: Worn spark plug overloading the coil

P0871.t: Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch C Circuit Range/Performance
P0871.m: A third transmission fluid pressure reading doesn't look right.

P0850.m: The park/neutral switch signal has a fault, so starting or idle control may act up.

P0846.t: Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch B Circuit Range/Performance
P0846.m: A second transmission fluid pressure reading doesn't look right.

P0193.t: Fuel Rail Pressure Sensor A Circuit High
P0193.m: The fuel pressure sensor signal is too high.

P207F.m: On a diesel, the computer decided the diesel exhaust fluid (DEF) is not cleaning the exhaust the way good fluid should. Emissions rise and, if not fixed, the truck may limit its speed or power.

P0491.t: Secondary Air Injection System Insufficient Flow (Bank 1)
P0491.m: The secondary air system isn't moving enough air on bank 1.

P205C.t: Reductant Tank Temperature Sensor Circuit Low
P205C.m: On a diesel, the sensor that reads the temperature of the diesel exhaust fluid tank is sending a voltage that is too low. The exhaust cleaning system may not work right and the check engine light comes on.
c: SCR control module or engine computer fault

P0513.m: The anti-theft system didn't recognize the key, so the engine may not start or may stall right away.

P2609.m: The intake air heater (used for cold starts) isn't performing as expected.

P203B.m: On a diesel, the reading from the diesel exhaust fluid level sensor does not make sense. The DEF gauge may be wrong or show low fluid when the tank is full.
c: Wrong fluid in the DEF tank

U0102.t: Lost Communication With Transfer Case Control Module
U0102.m: The other computers in the car stopped hearing from the transfer case module. Features that depend on it can stop working, and several warning lights often come on together.
c: Wiring or connector fault on the data network
Power or ground problem at the transfer case module

P2565.t: Turbocharger Boost Control Position Sensor Circuit High
P2565.m: The sensor that reports where the turbo's boost control is sits at a voltage that is too high. The engine may feel weak or hesitate, and fuel economy can drop.
c: Failed boost control position sensor (most common)

P0015.t: B Camshaft Position Timing Over-Retarded (Exhaust, Bank 1)
P0015.m: The variable valve timing for the exhaust camshaft on bank 1 isn't where the computer asked it to be. The engine can idle rough, lose power or use more fuel. Low or dirty oil is a common trigger, because oil pressure moves the timing.
c: Low, old or wrong-grade engine oil

P0100.t: Mass or Volume Air Flow Sensor A Circuit
P0100.m: The air flow sensor isn't reporting properly, so the computer guesses how much fuel to add.

P2813.t: Pressure Control Solenoid G Control Circuit Range/Performance
P2813.m: The transmission computer sees that pressure control solenoid G is not working the way it commands. Shifts may slip or feel harsh, and the transmission may go into limp mode or run hot.
c: Dirty or low transmission fluid, or clogged filter

P0A80.m: The hybrid battery has weak cells and the computer says it needs replacing. Power and mileage drop.

P050F.m: The computer sees too little vacuum in the brake booster, which helps you press the brake pedal. The pedal can feel hard and take more effort to stop the car.
c: Faulty one-way check valve or brake vacuum sensor

P0190.t: Fuel Rail Pressure Sensor A Circuit
P0190.m: The fuel pressure sensor has an electrical fault.

U0423.t: Invalid Data Received From Instrument Panel Control Module
U0423.m: Another computer in the car received data from the instrument panel module that did not make sense.
c: A fault inside the instrument panel module

P2450.t: Evaporative Emission System Switching Valve Performance/Stuck Open
P2450.m: An EVAP switching valve isn't working right.

P061C.t: Internal Control Module Engine RPM Performance
P061C.m: The engine computer's RPM check found a mismatch.

P219E.m: Cylinder 3 is getting a different air-fuel mix than the other cylinders.

U0452.t: Invalid Data Received From Restraints Control Module
U0452.m: Another computer in the car received data from the airbag (restraints) control module that did not make sense.
c: A fault inside the airbag (restraints) control module

P0867.m: Transmission fluid pressure isn't what the computer expects.

P2535.t: Ignition Switch Run/Start Position Circuit High
P2535.m: The ignition switch run/start circuit reads too high.

P0A1E.m: On a hybrid, the computer found a fault in the module that runs the motor-generator used to start the engine and charge the battery. The hybrid system may shut down or not work.

P0929.t: Gear Shift Lock Solenoid/Actuator Control Circuit Range/Performance
P0929.m: The shift lock (the part that keeps the shifter in park until you press the brake) isn't working right.

P04FB.t: Crankcase Ventilation Hose Connection Pressure Sensor Performance
P04FB.m: The computer uses a pressure sensor to check that the crankcase vent hose is connected and working, and that sensor's reading does not make sense. Usually only the check engine light comes on.
c: Water or ice from condensation in the sensor or hose (cold, short trips)
Disconnected, split or blocked vent hose

P04DB.m: The PCV hose that vents the engine crankcase looks disconnected.

P07F6.m: In 9th gear, the transmission's input and output speeds do not match the ratio 9th gear should give, so the computer thinks it is slipping or in the wrong gear. The driver may feel slipping, flare or harsh shifts.
c: Faulty shift solenoid or valve body

P0571.m: The brake pedal switch has a fault. Cruise control and brake lights may not work right.

P0785.m: The shift timing solenoid has a fault.

P0320.m: The computer lost the engine speed signal it uses to time the spark. The engine can stall or not start.
c: Failed crank or distributor pickup sensor

P0A7A.m: On a hybrid, the computer found that the inverter that controls the generator is not working as it should. The high-voltage hybrid system may shut down.

P0136.m: The downstream O2 sensor (after the catalytic converter) has a fault.

P2198.t: O2 Sensor Signal Biased/Stuck Rich (Bank 2 Sensor 1)
P2198.m: The bank 2 upstream O2 sensor keeps reading rich.

P2285.t: Injector Control Pressure Sensor Circuit Low
P2285.m: On engines that use oil pressure to fire the injectors (mainly diesels), the sensor that reads that oil pressure reads too low. The engine may be hard to start or not start.
c: Low oil level or oil pump problem
Damaged wiring, bad ground or corroded connector

P0120.m: The throttle position sensor signal has an electrical fault. The car may go into reduced power.

P0170.m: The computer had to adjust fuel on bank 1 beyond its normal range.

P0A3E.m: On a hybrid, the inverter that controls the generator is running too hot. The hybrid system may cut power to protect itself.
c: Low coolant in the inverter cooling loop
Clogged radiator or bad cooling fan

P0007.t: Fuel Shutoff Valve A Control Circuit High
P0007.m: The computer sees a voltage that is too high in the circuit that controls fuel shutoff valve A. The check engine light comes on; other symptoms depend on the engine.
c: Wiring shorted to voltage in the valve control circuit

P0204.m: The fuel injector circuit for cylinder 4 is open or faulty, so that cylinder may get no fuel and misfire.

P2431.t: Secondary Air Injection System Air Flow/Pressure Sensor Circuit Range/Performance (Bank 1)
P2431.m: The secondary air pressure sensor reading doesn't look right.

P2433.t: Secondary Air Injection System Air Flow/Pressure Sensor Circuit High (Bank 1)
P2433.m: The secondary air pressure sensor reads too high.

P0840.t: Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch A Circuit
P0840.m: A transmission fluid pressure switch has an electrical fault.

P0A7F.m: The hybrid battery is wearing out and storing less energy.

P2187.t: System Too Lean at Idle Bank 1
P2187.m: At idle, the engine on bank 1 is getting too much air for the fuel it gets. The idle may be rough, the engine can misfire, and it may be hard to start when hot.
c: Vacuum or intake air leak (hoses, brake booster line, PCV)
Dirty or faulty mass airflow sensor
Weak fuel pump, clogged filter or bad regulator

P0975.t: Shift Solenoid B Control Circuit Open
P0975.m: The circuit for shift solenoid B is open.

P2A00.m: The upstream O2 sensor signal is out of its expected range.

P0309.m: Cylinder 9 is not firing properly, so the engine runs rough and loses some power. A flashing check engine light means the misfire is serious enough to damage the catalytic converter, so slow down and get it checked right away.
c: Spark plug or ignition coil on cylinder 9

P0037.t: HO2S Heater Control Circuit Low (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
P0037.m: The downstream O2 sensor heater circuit reads too low.

P050B.m: Right after a cold start, the spark timing isn't where the computer wants it.

P06B8.t: Internal Control Module Non-Volatile Random Access Memory (NVRAM) Error
P06B8.m: The engine computer found an error in its saved memory.

P2422.t: Evaporative Emission System Vent Valve Stuck Closed
P2422.m: The EVAP vent valve is stuck shut, which can make it hard to fill the tank.

P0657.m: Power to some engine actuators is missing.

P0A08.m: The part that charges the 12-volt battery from the hybrid battery has a fault. The 12-volt battery can run down.

P2006.t: Intake Manifold Runner Control Stuck Closed (Bank 1)
P2006.m: The flaps inside the bank 1 intake manifold are stuck closed. Power and smoothness can suffer.
c: Carbon buildup on the runner flaps

P2263.m: The boost system isn't performing as expected.

P0713.t: Transmission Fluid Temperature Sensor A Circuit High
P0713.m: The transmission fluid temperature sensor reads as an open circuit.

U0126.t: Lost Communication With Steering Angle Sensor Module
U0126.m: The other computers in the car stopped hearing from the steering angle sensor module. Features that depend on it can stop working, and several warning lights often come on together.
c: Wiring or connector fault on the data network
Power or ground problem at the steering angle sensor module

P0117.t: Engine Coolant Temperature Sensor 1 Circuit Low
P0117.m: The coolant temperature sensor reads too low a voltage (looks extremely hot to the computer).

P000D.m: The bank 2 exhaust cam timing changes slower than commanded.

P26AB.t: Engine Coolant Bypass Valve A Stuck Open
P26AB.m: The coolant bypass (coolant control) valve is stuck open and does not move when the computer commands it. The engine and transmission may not hold the right temperature, and the check engine light comes on.
c: Engine computer software needs an update
Poor electrical connection at the valve

P0270.m: The computer sees a voltage that is too low in the circuit for the fuel injector on cylinder 4. The engine may run rough, lose power and use more fuel.
c: Open or short in the injector wiring

P0973.t: Shift Solenoid A Control Circuit Low
P0973.m: The circuit for shift solenoid A reads too low.

P2191.t: System Too Lean at Higher Load (Bank 1)
P2191.m: Bank 1 runs lean when you accelerate or pull hard.

U0212.t: Lost Communication With Steering Column Control Module
U0212.m: The other computers in the car stopped hearing from the steering column module. Features that depend on it can stop working, and several warning lights often come on together.
c: Wiring or connector fault on the data network
Power or ground problem at the steering column module

U0184.m: The other computers in the car stopped hearing from the radio. Features that depend on it can stop working, and several warning lights often come on together.
c: Wiring or connector fault on the data network
Power or ground problem at the radio

P0091.t: Fuel Pressure Regulator 1 Control Circuit Low
P0091.m: The fuel pressure control circuit reads too low (often a short to ground).

P0793.t: Intermediate Shaft Speed Sensor A Circuit No Signal
P0793.m: The transmission computer gets no signal from the sensor that measures the speed of the intermediate shaft. Shifts may be harsh, and other warning lights or limp mode may follow.

U0159.t: Lost Communication With Parking Assist Control Module
U0159.m: The other computers in the car stopped hearing from the parking assist module. Features that depend on it can stop working, and several warning lights often come on together.
c: Wiring or connector fault on the data network
Power or ground problem at the parking assist module

P05A0.t: Active Grille Air Shutter A Stuck On
P05A0.m: The movable shutters in the front grille that open and close to manage airflow are stuck and not moving as commanded. The check engine light comes on; warm-up can be slower, and in hot driving the engine may get less cooling air.
c: Ice, snow or debris blocking the shutters

P07B4.t: Transmission Park Position Sensor/Switch A Circuit High
P07B4.m: The sensor that tells the computer the transmission is in Park is sending a voltage that is too high. The car may not start, may be hard to shift out of Park, or the starter may work in the wrong gear.
c: Failed park position sensor or switch

P2007.t: Intake Manifold Runner Control Stuck Closed (Bank 2)
P2007.m: The flaps inside the bank 2 intake manifold are stuck closed. Power and smoothness can suffer.
c: Carbon buildup on the runner flaps

P0598.m: The electrically heated thermostat circuit reads too low.

P073F.m: The transmission was asked to go into 1st gear but the computer could not confirm that it did. The car may pull away weakly, go into limp mode or limit its speed.
c: Low, dirty or wrong transmission fluid

P04F0.t: EVAP System High Load Purge Line A Performance
P04F0.m: The fuel vapor system has a separate purge line used when a turbo engine is under boost, and the computer found that line is not working right. Usually only the check engine light comes on, sometimes with a fuel smell.
c: Cracked, disconnected or blocked purge line
Faulty purge valve or check valve
Damaged ejector (venturi) in the purge line

U0403.t: Invalid Data Received From Transfer Case Control Module
U0403.m: Another computer in the car received data from the transfer case module that did not make sense.
c: A fault inside the transfer case module

P018C.t: Fuel Pressure Sensor B Circuit Low
P018C.m: The second fuel pressure sensor (sensor B) is sending a voltage that is too low. The engine may be hard to start, not start, or feel weak.
c: Low fuel pressure from a weak pump or clogged filter

P0AE1.m: On a hybrid or EV, the computer found a fault with the precharge contactor, a relay that eases high voltage on gently before the main battery relays close. The car may not go into Ready mode or the hybrid system may shut off.
c: Failed precharge contactor or its resistor

U0104.t: Lost Communication With Cruise Control Module
U0104.m: The other computers in the car stopped hearing from the cruise control module. Features that depend on it can stop working, and several warning lights often come on together.
c: Wiring or connector fault on the data network
Power or ground problem at the cruise control module

P0B24.m: The high-voltage battery's voltage is jumping around more than it should. Power may be limited, fuel economy may drop, and the hybrid system may shut down.

P0689.t: ECM/PCM Power Relay Sense Circuit Low
P0689.m: The circuit the engine computer uses to check its main power relay reads too low. The car may be slow to start or not start, and some electrical items may not work.
c: Open or shorted wire between the relay and the computer

P2C7A.t: NOx Catalyst Efficiency Below Threshold Bank 1 Catalyst 2
P2C7A.m: On a diesel, the computer found that the second exhaust catalyst (the SCR catalyst that uses DEF) is not removing enough NOx. The check engine light comes on and emissions are higher.
c: Engine computer software issue (fixed by an update on some trucks)

P0BBE.m: The voltage differs too much between the sections of the high-voltage battery pack. Fuel economy and electric range may drop, and the hybrid system may limit power.
c: Weak or failing battery cells or modules

P2291.t: Injector Control Pressure Too Low - Engine Cranking
P2291.m: While the engine is cranking, the oil pressure used to fire the injectors (mainly on diesels) is too low, so the engine may not start. Smoke or odd engine noises can also show up.
c: Low engine oil level or oil pressure
Leak in the high-pressure oil system
Faulty injection pressure regulator or sensor

P2713.m: The transmission computer found a fault with pressure control solenoid D, which sets hydraulic pressure for shifting. Shifts may slip or feel harsh, and the transmission may go into limp mode or run hot.

P0207.m: The fuel injector circuit for cylinder 7 is open or faulty, so that cylinder may get no fuel and misfire.

P0208.m: The fuel injector circuit for cylinder 8 is open or faulty, so that cylinder may get no fuel and misfire.

P0205.m: The fuel injector circuit for cylinder 5 is open or faulty, so that cylinder may get no fuel and misfire.

P0103.t: Mass or Volume Air Flow Sensor A Circuit High
P0103.m: The air flow sensor signal is too high.

P0025.t: B Camshaft Position Timing Over-Retarded (Exhaust, Bank 2)
P0025.m: The variable valve timing for the exhaust camshaft on bank 2 isn't where the computer asked it to be. The engine can idle rough, lose power or use more fuel. Low or dirty oil is a common trigger, because oil pressure moves the timing.
c: Low, old or wrong-grade engine oil

P0020.t: A Camshaft Position Actuator Circuit (Intake, Bank 2)
P0020.m: The variable valve timing for the intake camshaft on bank 2 isn't where the computer asked it to be. The engine can idle rough, lose power or use more fuel. Low or dirty oil is a common trigger, because oil pressure moves the timing.
c: Low, old or wrong-grade engine oil

P2702.t: Transmission Friction Element C Apply Time Range/Performance
P2702.m: Clutch pack C inside the transmission takes too long (or too little time) to engage, so shifts can slip or flare.

P2700.t: Transmission Friction Element A Apply Time Range/Performance
P2700.m: Clutch pack A inside the transmission takes too long (or too little time) to engage, so shifts can slip or flare.

P0310.m: Cylinder 10 is not firing properly, so the engine runs rough and loses some power. A flashing check engine light means the misfire is serious enough to damage the catalytic converter, so slow down and get it checked right away.
c: Spark plug or ignition coil on cylinder 10

P0311.m: Cylinder 11 is not firing properly, so the engine runs rough and loses some power. A flashing check engine light means the misfire is serious enough to damage the catalytic converter, so slow down and get it checked right away.
c: Spark plug or ignition coil on cylinder 11

P0312.m: Cylinder 12 is not firing properly, so the engine runs rough and loses some power. A flashing check engine light means the misfire is serious enough to damage the catalytic converter, so slow down and get it checked right away.
c: Spark plug or ignition coil on cylinder 12

P0206.m: The fuel injector circuit for cylinder 6 is open or faulty, so that cylinder may get no fuel and misfire.

P0357.m: The computer sees an electrical fault in ignition coil G (usually the coil for cylinder 7). That cylinder may misfire. If the check engine light flashes, ease off and get it checked right away.
c: Worn spark plug overloading the coil

P0358.m: The computer sees an electrical fault in ignition coil H (usually the coil for cylinder 8). That cylinder may misfire. If the check engine light flashes, ease off and get it checked right away.
c: Worn spark plug overloading the coil

P0359.m: The computer sees an electrical fault in ignition coil I (usually the coil for cylinder 9). That cylinder may misfire. If the check engine light flashes, ease off and get it checked right away.
c: Worn spark plug overloading the coil

P0209.m: The fuel injector circuit for cylinder 9 is open or faulty, so that cylinder may get no fuel and misfire.

P0360.m: The computer sees an electrical fault in ignition coil J (usually the coil for cylinder 10). That cylinder may misfire. If the check engine light flashes, ease off and get it checked right away.
c: Worn spark plug overloading the coil

P0210.m: The fuel injector circuit for cylinder 10 is open or faulty, so that cylinder may get no fuel and misfire.

P0361.m: The computer sees an electrical fault in ignition coil K (usually the coil for cylinder 11). That cylinder may misfire. If the check engine light flashes, ease off and get it checked right away.
c: Worn spark plug overloading the coil

P0211.m: The fuel injector circuit for cylinder 11 is open or faulty, so that cylinder may get no fuel and misfire.

P0362.m: The computer sees an electrical fault in ignition coil L (usually the coil for cylinder 12). That cylinder may misfire. If the check engine light flashes, ease off and get it checked right away.
c: Worn spark plug overloading the coil

P0212.m: The fuel injector circuit for cylinder 12 is open or faulty, so that cylinder may get no fuel and misfire.

P0023.t: B Camshaft Position Actuator Circuit (Exhaust, Bank 2)
P0023.m: The variable valve timing for the exhaust camshaft on bank 2 isn't where the computer asked it to be. The engine can idle rough, lose power or use more fuel. Low or dirty oil is a common trigger, because oil pressure moves the timing.
c: Low, old or wrong-grade engine oil
